candidates.rationale: Both instructions describe feet-braced seated cable rows with a still torso and a pull toward the lower torso. The elevated version adds a secured box on the seat.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seat height and a secure support are setup details; retain the ordinary seated row movement.
candidates.name: Elevated Cable Rows
instructions: Use a seated cable row station with a low, stable box securely fixed on the seat to raise the sitting position. Use only a support that fits securely and is rated to support you.
Sit down on the machine and place your feet on the front platform or crossbar provided making sure that your knees are slightly bent and not locked.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.

With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched and your chest should be sticking out. You should be feeling a nice stretch on your lats as you hold the bar in front of you. This is the starting position of the exercise.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should be squeezing your back muscles hard. Hold that contraction for a second and slowly go back to the original position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit tall with feet braced and knees softly bent.
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs, then reach forward under control without rounding or rocking the torso.

candidates.variation: Bench used only as a depth target
candidates.rationale: Both descriptions use two dumbbells held at the sides and the same squat and return. The candidate replaces the ordinary depth instruction with a light touch on the bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Offer a stable bench as an optional depth cue; this is not the paused seated Box Squat.
candidates.name: Dumbbell Squat To A Bench
instructions: Stand up straight with a flat bench behind you while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the dumbbells as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both keep the feet planted and lower back steady while curling the shoulders a short distance. The candidate holds a plate at the chest; the base already supports optional load.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain optional plate loading and secure chest-level handling.
candidates.name: Weighted Crunches
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet planted, holding a weight plate securely against the chest.
Curl the shoulders a small distance off the floor while keeping the lower back steady.
Pause briefly and lower under control before repeating.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both are overhand pull-ups from extended arms, with a controlled lowering. The candidate adds a dip-belt weight; the base already has optional load tracking.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain dip-belt setup and added-weight entry; do not carry over forced back arching as a requirement.
candidates.name: Weighted Pull Ups
instructions: Attach a weight to a dip belt and secure it around your waist. Grab the pull-up bar with the palms of your hands facing forward. For a medium grip, your hands should be spaced at shoulder width. Both arms should be extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip.
You'll want to bring your torso back about 30 degrees while creating a curvature in your lower back and sticking your chest out. This will be your starting position.
Now, exhale and pull your torso up until your head is above your hands. Concentrate on squeezing yourshoulder blades back and down as you reach the top contracted position.
After a brief moment at the top contracted position, inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position with your arms extended and your lats fully stretched.
baseInstructions: Take an overhand grip on a secure pull-up bar.
Pull the elbows down until the chin clears the bar comfortably, then lower with control without swinging.

candidates.rationale: Both curl the shoulder blades a short distance from the floor with knees bent and feet planted. The candidate adds arms held overhead.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Overhead arms change leverage; offer the position as an optional form detail.
candidates.name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
instructions: Lie on the floor with your back flat and knees bent with around a 60-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and stretch your arms overhead with your palms crossed. This will be your starting position.

Curl your upper body forward and bring your shoulder blades just off the floor. At all times, keep your arms aligned with your head, neck and shoulder. Don't move them forward from that position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.variation: Bench/box touch as a coaching cue
candidates.rationale: The candidate says the bench teaches hip position and depth and instructs only a slight touch before standing. The base already covers the same barbell back squat.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional depth target and controlled touch; do not imply sitting, relaxing, or bouncing.
candidates.name: Barbell Squat To A Bench
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first place a flat bench or a box behind you. The flat bench is used to teach you to set your hips back and to hit depth.

Then, set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting your hips back as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.variation: Crossed arms plus bench depth target
candidates.rationale: The candidate is a front squat with crossed arms and a touch of the glutes to a bench; the base has the same front-rack load and squat/stand sequence.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Comfortable front-rack grip and optional depth target can be form choices.
candidates.name: Cross-Arm Front Squat to Bench
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set a flat bench behind you and set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you touch the bench with your glutes. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Support the bar on the front shoulders with elbows lifted and safeties set.
Sit between the hips while keeping the torso tall, then stand without allowing the elbows to drop.

candidates.rationale: Both keep a bar across the front shoulders with elbows raised and squat upright. The distinguishing instruction is crossing the arms over the bar.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Cross-arm grip may be an optional secure front-rack setup.
candidates.name: Cross-Arm Front Squat
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the middle of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Support the bar on the front shoulders with elbows lifted and safeties set.
Sit between the hips while keeping the torso tall, then stand without allowing the elbows to drop.

candidates.rationale: The candidate is the same barbell back squat but requires hamstrings to reach calves. The base already permits a comfortable depth.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Depth is a range option, not a requirement to force every user below their controlled range.
candidates.name: Barbell Full Squat
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.rationale: Both start hanging with extended arms and pull up under control. The candidate uses a V-bar attachment for a neutral grip instead of the base overhand bar grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Neutral grip and a securely rated attachment are setup options; the attachment must be stable.
candidates.name: V-Bar Pullup
instructions: Secure a suitable V-bar attachment over the pull-up bar so it is stable and rated for the intended hanging load. Take a neutral grip on its handles and hang with arms extended.
Pull upward under control, keeping the head clear of the bar and the trunk steady.
Lower slowly to the starting hang and repeat.
baseInstructions: Take an overhand grip on a secure pull-up bar.
Pull the elbows down until the chin clears the bar comfortably, then lower with control without swinging.

candidates.rationale: Both perform bilateral dumbbell curls with upper arms supported on a preacher pad. The candidate keeps the palms inward.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Neutral grip changes muscle emphasis and loading; retain the option if adopting a grip-neutral catalog.
candidates.name: Preacher Hammer Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand and the upper arms supported. Keep the palms facing one another.
Curl both dumbbells while maintaining the neutral grip and keeping the upper arms against the pad.
Extend the elbows to lower the forearms under control and repeat.
baseInstructions: Rest the upper arms fully on the preacher pad.
Curl the dumbbells without lifting the arms from the pad, then extend the elbows through a comfortable range.

candidates.rationale: Both put hands on a stable bench with feet back and lower the chest toward it. The candidate only specifies hands wider than shoulder width.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep bench stability and comfortable hand spacing in the base guidance.
candidates.name: Incline Push-Up Wide
instructions: Stand facing a stable bench that cannot slide or tip.
Place your hands on the bench, with your hands wider than shoulder width.
Position your feet back from the bench with arms and body straight. Your arms should be perpendicular to the body. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, lower your chest toward the bench by bending the arms.
Return to the starting position by extending the elbows, pressing yourself back up.
baseInstructions: Place the hands on a stable raised bench and step the feet back.
Lower the chest toward the support, then press away without letting the hips sag.

candidates.rationale: Both use a straight-body floor push-up and the same elbow bend/press. The candidate specifies wide hands; the base already allows hands under or just outside the shoulders.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain comfortable hand-width choice as a form option.
candidates.name: Push-Up Wide
instructions: With your hands wide apart, support your body on your toes and hands in a plank position. Your elbows should be extended and your body straight. Do not allow your hips to sag. This will be your starting position.
To begin, allow the elbows to flex, lowering your chest to the floor as you inhale.
Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position by extending the elbows. Exhale as you perform this step.
After pausing at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Place hands under or just outside the shoulders and form a straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows to lower the chest, then press the floor away without letting the hips sag.

candidates.rationale: The candidate describes only the first quarter of a sit-up, curling the torso up and down with arms crossed. That matches the base crunch; soles touching and knees apart are the added setup.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Butterfly leg position can be an optional comfort/setup cue.
candidates.name: Butterfly Crunch
instructions: Lie with your back flat on the floor (or exercise mat) and your legs extended in front of you.
Now bend at the knees and place your outer thighs by the floor (or mat) as you make the soles of your feet touch each other.

Now try pushing both soles and bringing them up as near you as possible while you keep the outer thighs on the floor (or at least almost touching it). Tip: In this position your legs should create a diamond shape.
Now, cross your arms in front of you by touching the opposite shoulders. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale flatten your lower back to the floor while curling the torso upwards. Tip: This will be like performing the first 1/4 movement of a sit up. Hold at the top position for a second.
As you inhale, slowly lower back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both keep the lower back on the floor and curl the shoulders up a few inches. The candidate rests the feet on a ball instead of the floor; the trunk is not on the ball.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional leg support and bent knees; distinguish this from Exercise Ball Crunch, which supports the torso on the ball.
candidates.name: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your feet resting on an exercise ball and your knees bent at a 90 degree angle.
Place your feet three to four inches apart and point your toes inward so they touch.
Place your hands lightly on either side of your head keeping your elbows in. Tip: Don't lock your fingers behind your head.
Keep the trunk controlled and the lower back comfortably supported. This will be your starting position.

Begin to roll your shoulders off the floor and keep the lower back comfortably supported. Your shoulders should come up off the floor only about four inches, and your lower back should remain on the floor. Breathe out as you execute this portion of the movement. Squeeze your abdominals hard at the top of the contraction and hold for a second. Tip: Focus on a slow, controlled movement. Refrain from using momentum at any time.
Slowly go back down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.variation: Low-incline label for an existing supported reverse fly
candidates.rationale: Both lie chest down on an incline bench, keep a fixed soft elbow bend and raise dumbbells out to the sides. The candidate specifies an approximately 15-degree incline.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Comfortable support angle and unchanged rear-delt raise path.
candidates.name: Low-Incline Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
instructions: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench.
Position the palms of the hands in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arms extended with the elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arms to the side until your elbows are at shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arms perpendicular to the torso while keeping them extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both lie on a bench and extend the elbows with the upper arms held steady. The candidate changes the lowering target from near the forehead to near the chin.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Use a comfortable path clear of the face; do not prescribe face contact.
candidates.name: Lying Barbell Triceps Press to Chin
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with the head and back supported. Hold a straight barbell above the upper chest using a comfortable overhand grip.
Keep the upper arms steady and bend the elbows to lower the bar toward the chin, stopping short of the face within a comfortable range.
Extend the elbows to return the bar above the chest, then repeat under control.
baseInstructions: Lie on a bench with a light bar above the chest.
Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward a comfortable point near the forehead, then extend the elbows without letting the shoulders drift.

candidates.rationale: Both use the same back-supported hack-squat machine, shoulder pads, knee/hip bend and return. The variant specifies feet about three inches apart instead of shoulder width.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Offer a comfortable stance cue without a separate exercise or mandatory narrow width.
candidates.name: Narrow Stance Hack Squats
instructions: Place the back of your torso against the back pad of the machine and hook your shoulders under the shoulder pads provided.

Position your legs in the platform using a less than shoulder width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Your feet should be around 3 inches or less apart. Tip: Keep your head up at all times and also maintain the back on the pad at all times.
Place your arms on the side handles of the machine and disengage the safety bars (which on most designs is done by moving the side handles from a facing front position to a diagonal position).
Now straighten your legs without locking the knees. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the unit by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up (back on the pad at all times). Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the unit as you exhale by pushing the floor with mainly with the heels of your feet as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Place the back of your torso against the back pad of the machine and hook your shoulders under the shoulder pads provided.
Position your legs in the platform using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Tip: Keep your head up at all times and also maintain the back on the pad at all times.
Place your arms on the side handles of the machine and disengage the safety bars (which on most designs is done by moving the side handles from a facing front position to a diagonal position).
Now straighten your legs without locking the knees. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the unit by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up (back on the pad at all times). Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the unit as you exhale by pushing the floor with mainly with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both lower and press the same leg-press platform with the back supported. The narrow version changes foot spacing, not the exercise sequence.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Foot placement can remain an optional form preference.
candidates.name: Narrow Stance Leg Press
instructions: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a less-than-shoulder-width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Your feet should be around 3 inches or less apart. Tip: Keep your head up at all times and also maintain the back on the pad at all times.

Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Make sure that you do not lock your knees. Your torso and the legs should make a perfect 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
Pushing mainly with the heels of your feet and using the quadriceps go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done. You do not want that platform falling on you fully loaded.
baseInstructions: Adjust the seat to keep the lower back supported throughout the movement.
Lower the sled through a comfortable knee bend, then press away without locking the knees forcefully.

candidates.rationale: Both are barbell back squats. The candidate prescribes feet 3–6 inches apart rather than a self-selected stable stance.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Personal stance choice; avoid imposing the narrow measurement universally.
candidates.name: Narrow Stance Squats
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a less-than-shoulder-width narrow stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Feet should be around 3-6 inches apart. Keep your head up at all times (looking down will get you off balance) and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.rationale: Both stand at a low cable and curl while the upper arms stay by the sides. The hammer version uses a rope with palms facing inward instead of the base underhand grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Neutral grip changes the forearm position and emphasis; preserve it as an option under the user’s grip-as-preference policy.
candidates.name: Cable Hammer Curls - Rope Attachment
instructions: Attach a rope attachment to a low pulley and stand facing the machine about 12 inches away from it.
Grasp the rope with a neutral (palms-in) grip and stand straight up keeping the natural arch of the back and your torso stationary.
Put your elbows in by your side and keep them there stationary during the entire movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move; not your upper arms. This will be your starting position.
Using your biceps, pull your arms up as you exhale until your biceps touch your forearms. Tip: Remember to keep the elbows in and your upper arms stationary.
After a 1 second contraction where you squeeze your biceps, slowly start to bring the weight back to the original position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.

candidates.variation: Neutral grip instead of palms-up grip
candidates.rationale: Both current instructions stand with one dumbbell in each hand and curl both together while keeping the upper arms still. Hammer Curl maintains palms inward; Dumbbell Bicep Curl maintains palms forward. Under the stated grip-as-choice policy, this can be one exercise with a grip option.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Neutral grip changes forearm/elbow-flexor emphasis and load tolerance. Retain Hammer Curl as a search alias and grip option rather than erasing the technique choice.
candidates.name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing inward.
Curl both weights together without moving the upper arms forward, then lower slowly while keeping the same grip.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.variation: Neutral grip on the same incline curl
candidates.rationale: Both use a supported incline bench, hanging dumbbells and stationary upper arms for the same bilateral elbow curl. The hammer version keeps the palms inward; the ordinary incline curl turns them forward.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep the incline setup and neutral-grip option with its different load tolerance; this is not a proposal to merge incline curls with standing curls.
candidates.name: Incline Hammer Curls
instructions: Seat yourself on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand. You should pressed firmly against he back with your feet together. Allow the dumbbells to hang straight down at your side, holding them with a neutral grip. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by flexing at the elbow, attempting to keep the upper arm stationary.
Continue to the top of the movement and pause, then slowly return to the start position.
baseInstructions: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand held at arms length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both describe consecutive two-foot forward hops over a spaced row of small barriers, rebounding from each landing. The difference is cones versus hurdles; both already allow other small barriers.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep cones as a valid equipment alternative and retain per-hop tracking.
candidates.name: Front Cone Hops (or hurdle hops)
instructions: Set up a row of cones or other small barriers, placing them a few feet apart.
Stand in front of the first cone with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Begin by jumping with both feet over the first cone, swinging both arms as you jump.
Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next cone.
Continue until you have jumped over all of the cones.
baseInstructions: Set up a row of hurdles or other small barriers, placing them a few feet apart.
Stand in front of the first hurdle with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Begin by jumping with both feet over the first hurdle, swinging both arms as you jump.
Absorb the impact of landing by bending the knees, rebounding out of the first leap by jumping over the next hurdle. Continue until you have jumped over all of the hurdles.

candidates.variation: Over-specified name for the same setup
candidates.rationale: Both sit on a bench at a low cable, use a palms-up bar grip, support the forearms on the thighs with wrists beyond the knees, and move only the wrists.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: No material movement difference found; preserve old title as a search alias.
candidates.name: Seated Two-Arm Palms-Up Low-Pulley Wrist Curl
instructions: Put a bench in front of a low pulley machine that has a barbell or EZ Curl attachment on it.
Move the bench far enough away so that when you bring the handle to the top of your thighs tension is created on the cable due to the weight stack being moved up.
Now hold the handle with both hands, palms up, using a shoulder-width grip.
Step back and sit on the bench with your feet about shoulder width apart, firmly on the floor.
Lean forward and place the forearms on your thighs with the back of your wrists over your knees. This will be your starting position.
Lower the bar as far as possible, while inhaling and keeping a tight grip.
Now curl the bar up as high as possible while contracting the forearms. Tip: Only the wrist should move; not the forearms.
After a second contraction at the top go back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Start out by placing a flat bench in front of a low pulley cable that has a straight bar attachment.

Use your arms to grab the cable bar with a narrow to shoulder width supinated grip (palms up) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the top of your thighs. Your wrists should be hanging just beyond your knees.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling. Keep the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both use a low cable, stationary upper arms by the torso, and elbow flexion followed by a controlled return. The reverse version changes the bar grip from underhand to overhand.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve overhand grip as an option and do not imply identical forearm emphasis or loads.
candidates.name: Reverse Cable Curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley using a pronated (palms down) and shoulder width grip. Make sure also that you keep the elbows close to the torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the muscle.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both stand and curl a barbell with the upper arms still. The difference is a pronated instead of underhand grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Grip changes forearm/biceps emphasis and loading capacity; retain as a documented grip option if consolidated.
candidates.name: Reverse Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at shoulder width with the elbows close to the torso. The palm of your hands should be facing down (pronated grip). This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the muscle.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with an underhand grip on the bar.
Bend the elbows while keeping the upper arms near the sides, then lower without swinging the torso.

candidates.rationale: Both use an EZ bar with upper arms on a preacher pad and the same elbow flexion/extension. Only the specified grip orientation differs.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the grip option and its different load tolerance.
candidates.name: Reverse EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench and hold an EZ bar with a palms-down grip, keeping the upper arms supported on the pad.
Curl the bar without lifting the upper arms from the support.
Extend the elbows to lower the forearms through a comfortable range, then repeat.
baseInstructions: Sit at a preacher bench and hold an EZ bar with a comfortable underhand grip, keeping the upper arms supported on the pad.
Curl the bar without lifting the upper arms.
Extend the elbows to lower the forearms through a comfortable range and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both stand and curl two dumbbells without moving the upper arms. The candidate maintains an overhand grip instead of an underhand grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Grip orientation affects emphasis and weight tolerance; preserve as an option.
candidates.name: Standing Dumbbell Reverse Curl
instructions: To begin, stand straight with a dumbbell in each hand using a pronated grip (palms facing down). Your arms should be fully extended while your feet are shoulder width apart from each other. This is the starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the muscle.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: The candidate is the same standing bilateral dumbbell shoulder press while insisting that the palms stay inward.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Comfortable neutral grip can be offered in the standard press.
candidates.name: Standing Palms-In Dumbbell Press
instructions: Start by having a dumbbell in each hand with your arm fully extended to the side using a neutral grip. Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. Now slowly lift the dumbbells up until you create a 90 degree angle with your arms. Note: Your forearms should be perpendicular to the floor. This the starting position.
Continue to maintain a neutral grip throughout the entire exercise. Slowly lift the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended.
While inhaling lower the weights down until your arm is at a 90 degree angle again.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold the dumbbells beside the shoulders, with wrists stacked over elbows.
Press both dumbbells overhead without arching the back, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both set the seated handles near the middle chest and press forward by extending the elbows. The leverage version specifies loading plates on pins.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain plate-loaded versus selectorized setup cues; the movement can share Machine Chest Press.
candidates.name: Leverage Chest Press
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height. The handles should be near the bottom or middle of the pectorals at the beginning of the motion.
Your chest and head should be up and your shoulder blades retracted. This will be your starting position.
Press the handles forward by extending through the elbow.
After a brief pause at the top, return the weight just above the start position, keeping tension on the muscles by not returning the weight to the stops until the set is complete.
baseInstructions: Adjust the seat so the handles align with the middle of the chest.
Keep the back supported as you press forward and return under control.

candidates.rationale: Both sit with handles near the shoulders, press upward by extending the elbows, and lower back. The leverage version specifies plate loading.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Simplify the surviving title to Machine Shoulder Press; keep machine-specific seat and loading adjustments.
candidates.name: Leverage Shoulder Press
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat for your height. The handles should be near the top of the shoulders at the beginning of the motion. Your chest and head should be up and handles held with a pronated grip. This will be your starting position.
Press the handles upward by extending through the elbow.
After a brief pause at the top, return the weight to just above the start position, keeping tension on the muscles by not returning the weight to the stops until the set is complete.
baseInstructions: Sit down on the Shoulder Press Machine and select the weight.
Grab the handles to your sides as you keep the elbows bent and in line with your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now lift the handles as you exhale and you extend the arms fully. At the top of the position make sure that you hold the contraction for a second.
Lower the handles slowly back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both already describe a seated curl machine with upper arms against a pad, forearms flexing at the elbows, then a slow return.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Pad adjustment and stationary upper-arm cues belong in the shared machine curl guidance.
candidates.name: Machine Preacher Curls
instructions: Sit down on the Preacher Curl Machine and select the weight.

Place the back of your upper arms (your triceps) on the preacher pad provided and grab the handles using an underhand grip (palms facing up). Tip: Make sure that when you place the arms on the pad you keep the elbows in. This will be your starting position.

Now lift the handles as you exhale and you contract the biceps. At the top of the position make sure that you hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Only the forearms should move. The upper arms should remain stationary and on the pad at all times.
Lower the handles slowly back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Adjust the seat to the appropriate height and make your weight selection. Place your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by flexing the elbow, pulling your lower arm towards your upper arm.
Pause at the top of the movement, and then slowly return the weight to the starting position.
Avoid returning the weight all the way to the stops until the set is complete to keep tension on the muscles being worked.

candidates.rationale: Both start supine with knees bent and feet planted, lift the hips, then lower. The candidate adds a gentle pelvic tilt before the same bridge.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the tilt cue as optional setup rather than a separate exercise.
candidates.name: Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge
instructions: Lie on the back with knees bent and feet planted. Gently tilt the pelvis so the lower back settles toward the floor.
Press through the feet to lift the hips into a comfortable bridge without arching the back.
Lower the hips under control to the floor and release the tilt before repeating.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Press through the feet to lift the hips until the trunk and thighs align, then lower without arching the lower back.

candidates.variation: Rack bar instead of bench hand support
candidates.rationale: Both place the hands on a raised support and perform the same straight-body incline push-up. The candidate uses a secured rack bar rather than a stable bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support height, grip and bar security are setup options.
candidates.name: Rack-Bar Incline Push-Up
instructions: Secure a barbell in a squat rack at a height that allows a controlled incline push-up. Check that the bar cannot roll or shift.
Place your hands on the bar with a secure comfortable grip.
Position your feet back from the bar with arms and body straight. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your body straight, lower your chest to the bar by bending the arms.
Return to the starting position by extending the elbows, pressing yourself back up.
baseInstructions: Place the hands on a stable raised bench and step the feet back.
Lower the chest toward the support, then press away without letting the hips sag.

candidates.rationale: The candidate is a shallow bodyweight squat; the base already asks for a comfortable squat range with grounded feet. No new equipment, sequence, or loading is introduced.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Allow limited comfortable depth as a base form adjustment.
candidates.name: Partial Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Stand with the feet comfortably apart and the arms in front for balance.
Bend the hips and knees into a shallow squat, stopping above parallel while keeping both feet grounded.
Stand smoothly to complete one repetition. Repeat for the selected target.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet at a comfortable width.
Sit the hips down between the legs, keeping the whole foot grounded, then stand tall through a comfortable range.

candidates.rationale: Both lie on a flat bench and lower a bar to the chest before pressing back up. The candidate adds a supinated grip and tucked elbows, rather than a different exercise sequence.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: If retained as an option, preserve secure unracking and comfortable wrist/elbow position.
candidates.name: Reverse Triceps Bench Press
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a close, supinated grip (around shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked extended in front of you and perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest. Tip: Make sure that as opposed to a regular bench press, you keep the elbows close to the torso at all times in order to maximize triceps involvement.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your triceps muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
baseInstructions: Set the bench and rack safeties before lifting. Lie with feet planted, hands slightly wider than shoulders, and shoulder blades supported.
Unrack the bar over the chest. Lower it under control to a comfortable chest-level position.
Press back to the starting position, then return the bar securely to the rack after the set.

candidates.rationale: Both lie supine with upper arms perpendicular to the torso and extend only the elbows against a low cable. The variant uses a rope and the seat of a row station instead of a flat bench and bar.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Attachment and stable bench setup; preserve the lying extension position.
candidates.name: Low Cable Triceps Extension
instructions: Select the desired weight and lay down face up on the bench of a seated row machine that has a rope attached to it. Your head should be pointing towards the attachment.
Grab the outside of the rope ends with your palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Position your elbows so that they are bent at a 90 degree angle and your upper arms are perpendicular (90 degree angle) to your torso. Tip: Keep the elbows in and make sure that the upper arms point to the ceiling while your forearms point towards the pulley above your head. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, extend your lower arms until they are straight and vertical. The upper arms and elbows remain stationary throughout the movement. Only the forearms should move. Contract the triceps hard for a second.
As you breathe in slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Place a flat bench in front of a low pulley with its straight-bar attachment within reach. Take a narrow overhand grip on the bar before carefully lying back on the bench.
With your arms extended, position the bar over your torso. Your arms and your torso should create a 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.

Lower the bar by bending at the elbow while keeping the upper arms stationary and elbows in. Go down until the bar lightly touches your forehead. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Flex the triceps as you lift the bar back to its starting position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Hold for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both keep the elbows nearly straight and move at the shoulders to draw a high cable toward the thighs. The distinctive item is the rope.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename the surviving display name to Straight-Arm Pulldown and include rope/bar options if approved.
candidates.name: Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and make your weight selection. Stand a couple feet back from the pulley with your feet staggered and take the rope with both hands. Lean forward from the hip, keeping your back straight, with your arms extended up in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, extend the shoulder to pull the rope down to your thighs.
Pause at the bottom of the motion, squeezing your lats.
Return to the starting position without allowing the weight to fully rest on the stack.
baseInstructions: Face a high cable pulley fitted with a straight bar. Grasp it with a comfortable overhand grip, step back and keep the elbows softly extended.
Move at the shoulders to draw the bar toward the thighs, keeping the elbow angle and torso steady.
Return the arms overhead under control without letting the weight pull the back into an arch.

candidates.variation: Smith bar used only as hand support
candidates.rationale: Both hold the body straight with hands on a raised support, lower the chest toward that support, and press away. The Smith bar is not a moving resistance.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A bar must be secured against rotation; support height adjusts difficulty within Incline Push-Up.
candidates.name: Smith-Bar Incline Push-Up
instructions: Lock a Smith bar at a height that permits a controlled incline push-up and check that it cannot rotate free during the movement.
Grasp the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, step the feet back and keep the body in a steady line. Bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the bar.
Press away until the arms extend, maintaining the same body position. Count the lowering and press as one repetition.
baseInstructions: Place the hands on a stable raised bench and step the feet back.
Lower the chest toward the support, then press away without letting the hips sag.

candidates.rationale: Both instructions describe a controlled barbell shrug with straight arms and no leg drive. The candidate changes to a wide snatch grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Grip choice and secure bar handling; no ballistic clean/snatch pull is involved.
candidates.name: Snatch Shrug
instructions: Stand with a wide snatch grip on a barbell at the thighs, arms extended and trunk braced.
Raise the shoulders in a controlled shrug without bending the elbows or driving through the legs.
Lower the shoulders slowly to reset and repeat.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar at the thighs and arms straight.
Lift the shoulders toward the ears without rolling them, pause, and lower slowly.

candidates.rationale: Both hinge over and row a straight barbell to the torso. The candidate performs the row while standing on a bench, with the bar initially on it.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The elevated setup is unnecessary for the standard row; do not carry bench-standing into default instructions.
candidates.name: Straight Bar Bench Mid Rows
instructions: Place a loaded barbell on the end of a bench. Standing on the bench behind the bar, take a medium, pronated grip. Stand with your hips back and chest up, maintaining a neutral spine. This will be your starting position.
Row the bar to your torso by retracting the shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Use a controlled movement with no jerking.
After a brief pause, slowly return the bar to the starting position, ensuring to go all the way down.
baseInstructions: Hinge at the hips with knees softly bent and a steady trunk.
Pull the bar toward the lower ribs, pause, and lower without jerking the torso upward.

candidates.rationale: Both place a bar across the upper back and hinge at the hips with a steady trunk. The candidate uses softly extended knees instead of the base's slightly bent knees.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: A soft knee bend and controlled hip hinge; do not enforce locked knees.
candidates.name: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning
instructions: Take a barbell onto the upper back from a squat rack and step back into a balanced stance with knees softly extended.
Keep the head aligned with the trunk and hinge forward at the hips only as far as the back stays steady.
Return upright under control and rerack securely after the selected repetitions.
baseInstructions: Begin with a bar on a rack at shoulder height. Rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your shoulders. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Step back from the rack.
Begin by bending at the hips, moving them back as you bend over to near parallel. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Reverse the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings. Continue until you have returned to the starting position.

candidates.variation: Stiff-legged name for the same authored hinge
candidates.rationale: The current instructions for both begin standing with the bar near the thighs, keep a soft knee bend, hinge with the bar close and stop before back position changes. The candidate does not describe a floor reset.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Maintain a nearly steady knee angle; this conclusion follows the current catalog instructions, not every possible use of the exercise name.
candidates.name: Stiff-Legged Barbell Deadlift
instructions: Stand holding a barbell in front of the thighs with an overhand grip. Keep a small steady bend in the knees.
Hinge forward at the hips while keeping the bar close and the torso controlled. Stop at a comfortable hamstring stretch before the back position changes.
Extend the hips to return to standing. Keep the knee angle nearly unchanged throughout.
baseInstructions: Hold the bar near the thighs with knees softly bent.
Push the hips back while keeping the bar close, then drive the hips forward to stand before the back begins to round.

candidates.rationale: Both stand at a high cable and extend the elbows with upper arms beside the torso. The base uses a rope while the variant uses a straight bar.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename the surviving display name to Cable Triceps Pushdown and include compatible attachment choices if approved.
candidates.name: Straight-Bar Triceps Pushdown
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high cable and take an overhand grip. Stand with the upper arms beside the torso and elbows bent.
Keep the upper arms still and extend the elbows to press the bar downward.
Return under control to the bent-elbow start and repeat.
baseInstructions: Stand facing a high cable with a rope attachment and elbows beside the ribs.
Straighten the elbows to press the rope down, then return without moving the upper arms.

candidates.rationale: Both secure the thighs, pull an overhead cable bar toward the upper chest and extend the arms again. The variant prescribes a supinated, closer grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Grip orientation and width should be selectable guidance under Lat Pulldown.
candidates.name: Underhand Cable Pulldowns
instructions: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.
Grab the pull-down bar with the palms facing your torso (a supinated grip). Make sure that the hands are placed closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

As you breathe out, pull the bar down until it touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the fully contracted position and keep the elbows close to your body. The upper torso should remain stationary as your bring the bar to you and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, while breathing in, slowly bring the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Secure the thigh pad and grip the overhead bar.
Pull the bar toward the upper chest while keeping the torso mostly still, then let the arms extend under control.

candidates.rationale: Both are seated cable pulldowns toward the upper chest with thighs secured and torso steady. The V-bar version specifies a neutral-grip handle.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Compatible attachment choice and comfortable grip; equipment load histories may differ.
candidates.name: V-Bar Pulldown
instructions: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a V-Bar attached to the top pulley.
Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.

Grab the V-bar with the palms facing each other (a neutral grip). Stick your chest out and lean yourself back slightly (around 30-degrees) in order to better engage the lats. This will be your starting position.

Using your lats, pull the bar down as you squeeze your shoulder blades. Continue until your chest nearly touches the V-bar. Exhale as you execute this motion. Tip: Keep the torso stationary throughout the movement.
After a second hold on the contracted position, slowly bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Secure the thigh pad and grip the overhead bar.
Pull the bar toward the upper chest while keeping the torso mostly still, then let the arms extend under control.

candidates.rationale: Both press a high cable down by extending the elbows while holding the upper arms still by the torso. The V-bar changes the attachment and hand angle.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Use the same proposed generic Cable Triceps Pushdown base; do not retain an attachment-specific title.
candidates.name: Triceps Pushdown - V-Bar Attachment
instructions: Attach a V-Bar to a high pulley and grab with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width.

Standing upright with the torso straight and a very small inclination forward, bring the upper arms close to your body and perpendicular to the floor. The forearms should be pointing up towards the pulley as they hold the bar. The thumbs should be higher than the small finger. This is your starting position.

Using the triceps, bring the bar down until it touches the front of your thighs and the arms are fully extended perpendicular to the floor. The upper arms should always remain stationary next to your torso and only the forearms should move. Exhale as you perform this movement.
After a second hold at the contracted position, bring the V-Bar slowly up to the starting point. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand facing a high cable with a rope attachment and elbows beside the ribs.
Straighten the elbows to press the rope down, then return without moving the upper arms.

candidates.rationale: The same rack setup, bar position and squat/stand sequence differ by a wider-than-shoulder-width stance.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Comfortable stance width and knee tracking.
candidates.name: Wide Stance Barbell Squat
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a wider-than-shoulder-width stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance, and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.variation: Added band added to the standard lift
candidates.rationale: The candidate retains the EZ-Bar Curl movement and adds a band to the bar or setup. The base supplies the same main movement without that loading accessory.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve changing resistance/assistance, anchor setup and load notation as optional modifiers; bar weight alone is not comparable across setups.
candidates.name: EZ-Bar Curl with Band
instructions: Attach a band to each end of the bar. Take the bar, placing a foot on the middle of the band. Stand upright with a comfortable grip on the EZ bar. The elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the upper arms in place, flex the elbows to execute the curl. Exhale as the weight is lifted.
Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight while holding an EZ curl bar at the wide outer handle. The palms of your hands should be facing forward and slightly tilted inward due to the shape of the bar. Keep your elbows close to your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now, while keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps. Focus on only moving your forearms.
Continue to raise the weight until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the top contracted position for a moment and squeeze the biceps.
Then inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Despite its name, the candidate instructions describe a backward lunge plus a torso rotation across the front leg, not a separate crossover step. The base uses the same backward lunge without the twist.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep optional torso rotation distinct from the standard base cue; normalize per-side versus total repetition accounting.
candidates.name: Crossover Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Perform a rear lunge by stepping back with one foot and flexing the hips and front knee. As you do so, rotate your torso across the front leg.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position and repeat on the other side, continuing in an alternating fashion.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Step one foot backward and bend both knees through a comfortable range.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then alternate legs.
Each backward step and return counts as one repetition; enter the total across both sides.

candidates.rationale: Both use overhand pull-ups from a controlled hang. The candidate alternates ordinary pull-ups with a behind-the-head path; no new apparatus or independent movement family is introduced.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the retired name as an alias if wanted; do not make the special behind-head path part of the default pull-up demonstration.
candidates.name: Rocky Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from a secure pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip and a steady trunk.

Pull up in front of the bar on one repetition, then lower under control. On the next repetition, follow the behind-the-head path only through a comfortable controlled range without forcing the neck forward or touching it to the bar.
Alternate the two paths, counting each ascent and descent as one repetition.
baseInstructions: Take an overhand grip on a secure pull-up bar.
Pull the elbows down until the chin clears the bar comfortably, then lower with control without swinging.

candidates.variation: Angled raise path with thumbs upward

baseInstructions: Cross your arms over your chest.

Return to the starting position be driving through with the hips to come back to a standing position.
baseInstructions: Using a 41 inch band, stand on one end, spreading your feet a small amount. Bend at the hips to loop the end of the band behind your neck. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your legs straight, extend through the hips to come to a near vertical position.

candidates.rationale: Both shrug a straight-armed barbell by lifting the shoulders. The candidate carries the bar behind the back rather than in front of the thighs.

Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips as much as possible. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Lower bar position necessitates a greater torso lean to keep the bar over the heels. Continue until you break parallel, which is defined as the crease of the hip being in line with the top of the knee.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe, until you have returned to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.rationale: Both are soft-knee barbell hip hinges from the thighs with a stop before the back changes position. The candidate adds a low stable platform for potential extra range.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Platform height and controlled range; a deficit should not force the bar to the floor.
candidates.name: Romanian Deadlift from Deficit
instructions: Stand on a low stable lifting platform with a barbell held near the thighs. Use a height and load that allow controlled access to the starting position.
With the knees softly bent, hinge at the hips and keep the bar close to the legs. Stop when further lowering would change the back position; the bar does not need to reach the floor.
Drive through the feet and extend the hips to stand. Lower the bar and step off the platform under control at the end.
baseInstructions: Hold the bar near the thighs with knees softly bent.
Push the hips back while keeping the bar close, then drive the hips forward to stand before the back begins to round.

candidates.rationale: Both use a Smith bar across the upper back and squat through hip and knee flexion. Despite its name, the chair version has no chair: it chiefly moves the feet about 18 inches forward.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Foot placement changes torso and knee mechanics; keep it as optional coaching rather than silently imposing the same stance.
candidates.name: Smith Machine Chair Squat
instructions: To begin, first set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the bar is loaded, step under it and position it across the back of your shoulders.
Take the bar with your hands facing forward, unlock it and lift it off the rack by extending your legs.

Move your feet forward about 18 inches in front of the bar. Position your legs using a shoulder width stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Look forward at all times and maintain a neutral or slightly arched spine. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper and lower leg breaks 90 degrees.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heels of your feet, extending the knees and returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: To begin, first set the bar on the height that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side (palms facing forward), unlock it and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Keep your feet grounded and your knees tracking in line with your feet.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both sit with knees bent, lean back slightly, and rotate the trunk gently side to side. The candidate secures the feet; the base simply grounds the heels.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep foot anchoring as an optional support choice and retain a consistent per-side repetition convention.
candidates.name: Anchored-Foot Russian Twist
instructions: Sit with the knees bent and both feet secured under a stable purpose-built foot anchor. Lean the torso back slightly and extend the hands forward.
Rotate the trunk gently to one side, return through center and turn to the other side while keeping the pelvis steady.
Count each side turn and return as one repetition toward the total target. Use a comfortable controlled range.
baseInstructions: Sit with knees bent and heels grounded.
Lean back slightly with the spine long and rotate the chest a little to one side, then the other, keeping the movement controlled.
Count each turn to one side as one repetition; the entered count is the total across both directions.

candidates.variation: Forearms on thighs instead of bench
candidates.rationale: Both use two dumbbells and palms down to lift the backs of the hands. The candidate sits with forearms on thighs; the base kneels with forearms on a bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support choice is optional; preserve the same wrist-extension direction.
candidates.name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
instructions: Start out by placing two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench.
Sit down on the edge of the flat bench with your legs at about shoulder width apart. Make sure to keep your feet on the floor.

Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against your thighs with the palms of the hands facing down. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge of your thighs.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.

Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise. Tip: Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
When finished, simply lower the dumbbells to the floor.
baseInstructions: Kneel facing a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Rest the forearms on the bench with palms downward and wrists just beyond the edge.
Lift the backs of both hands, then lower through a small controlled range.

candidates.variation: Forearms on thighs instead of bench
candidates.rationale: Both use two dumbbells and palms up for supported wrist flexion. The candidate sits with forearms on thighs; the base kneels at the bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support choice is optional; preserve the same palm-up wrist-flexion direction.
candidates.name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
instructions: Start out by placing two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench.
Sit down on the edge of the flat bench with your legs at about shoulder width apart. Make sure to keep your feet on the floor.

Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against your thighs with the palms of the hands facing up. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge of your thighs.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.
