Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise. Tip: Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
When finished, simply lower the dumbbells to the floor.
baseInstructions: Kneel facing a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Rest the forearms on the bench with palms upward and wrists just beyond the edge.
Curl both wrists through a small controlled range, then lower the dumbbells slowly.

candidates.variation: Forearms supported on bench instead of thighs
candidates.rationale: Both are overhand barbell wrist extensions with still forearms. The candidate kneels at a bench while the base sits with forearms on the thighs.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Stable support and wrists free to move; preserve reverse wrist extension separately from palm-up flexion.
candidates.name: Palms-Down Wrist Curl Over A Bench
instructions: Start out by placing a barbell on one side of a flat bench.
Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.
Use your arms to grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms down) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the flat bench. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.
Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit on a bench with a barbell in an overhand grip and forearms supported on the thighs, wrists free just beyond the knees.
Lift the backs of the hands while keeping the forearms still.
Lower the bar under control through a comfortable wrist range and repeat.

candidates.variation: Forearms supported on bench instead of thighs
candidates.rationale: Both are underhand barbell wrist curls with still forearms. The candidate kneels at a bench while the base sits with forearms on the thighs.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Choose a stable forearm support; the wrist movement is unchanged despite the whole-body setup.
candidates.name: Palms-Up Barbell Wrist Curl Over A Bench
instructions: Start out by placing a barbell on one side of a flat bench.
Kneel down on both of your knees so that your body is facing the flat bench.
Use your arms to grab the barbell with a supinated grip (palms up) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the flat bench. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.
Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit on a bench with a barbell in an underhand grip and forearms supported on the thighs, wrists free just beyond the knees.
Curl the wrists upward while keeping the forearms still.
Lower the bar through a comfortable wrist range and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both hold a kettlebell overhead and hinge sideways with feet turned away from the loaded side. The advanced version places the free arm behind the back rather than leaving it free for balance/reach.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Extra balance demand is optional; keep the ordinary windmill as the default.
candidates.name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Clean and press one kettlebell overhead, keeping the wrist stacked above the shoulder. Turn the feet away from the loaded side and place the free arm behind the back.
Hinge at the hips while keeping the loaded arm upright and the torso controlled. Move only as far as you can maintain this position comfortably.
Drive through the feet to return to standing without bending the loaded elbow. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Place a kettlebell in front of your lead foot and clean and press it overhead with your opposite arm. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so, so that the palm faces forward. Press it overhead by extending the elbow.

Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the locked out kettlebell. Bending at the hip to one side, sticking your butt out, slowly lean only as far as you can maintain the loaded arm upright and the torso controlled. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell that you hold over your head at all times.
Pause for a second at the end of the comfortable reach and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.rationale: Both stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs and raise forward with a steady torso and unchanged soft elbow bend. The candidate continues overhead; the base stops around shoulder height.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Overhead range is a meaningful optional progression and requires controlled shoulder/trunk position; retain the standard shoulder-height default.
candidates.name: Standing Dumbbell Straight-Arm Front Delt Raise Above Head
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs and a steady trunk.
Maintain the same soft elbow angle as you raise the arms forward and overhead through a comfortable shoulder range.
Lower under control without locking the elbows or arching the back, then repeat.
baseInstructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, with the trunk steady.
Raise both arms together in front to about shoulder height, then lower slowly without leaning back.

candidates.rationale: Both front-squat with the bar supported on the shoulders. The candidate extends the arms forward without gripping the bar to teach rack position.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: It is explicitly a technique drill with a more demanding balance setup; keep that optional drill context.
candidates.name: Frankenstein Squat
instructions: This drill teaches you the proper positioning of both the bar and your body during the clean and front squat.

Place the barbell on the front of the shoulders, releasing your grip and extending your arms out in front of you. The shoulders should be pushed forward to create a shelf, and the bar should be in contact with the throat. Ensure that you only move your shoulder blades forward; don't round the thoracic spine.

Squat by flexing the knees and hips, sitting in between your legs. Keep the torso upright, the arms up, and the shoulders forward, and the bar should stay in place. Go to the bottom of the squat, until your hamstrings contact your calves.
Return to the upright position by driving through the front of the heel and extending the knees and hips.
baseInstructions: Support the bar on the front shoulders with elbows lifted and safeties set.
Sit between the hips while keeping the torso tall, then stand without allowing the elbows to drop.

candidates.variation: Incline bench instead of preacher-bench chest support
candidates.rationale: Both are chest-supported straight-bar curls with the arms hanging and elbows held still. The candidate uses an incline bench; Spider Curl uses the chest side of a preacher support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support angle and enough bar clearance; both are supported curls, not a standing barbell curl.
candidates.name: Barbell Curls Lying Against An Incline
instructions: Lie against an incline bench, with your arms holding a barbell and hanging down vertically toward the floor. This will be your starting position.

While keeping the upper arms stationary, curl the weight up as high as you can while squeezing the biceps. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Do not swing the arms.
After a second contraction, slowly go back to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Make sure that you go all of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lean chest down against the preacher bench support and take a straight barbell from secure reachable rests or a controlled handoff. Let the arms hang with a comfortable underhand grip.
Curl the bar while keeping the upper arms still and the chest supported.
Lower under control and return the bar to its support after the selected repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both keep the elbow angle fixed and pull a high cable toward the thighs by moving at the shoulders. The variant lies back on an incline bench rather than standing facing the cable.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Bench angle and orientation change the resistance relationship; retain a supported setup note if consolidated.
candidates.name: Incline Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
instructions: Place an incline bench facing away from a high cable pulley. Lie back on the bench and hold the bar overhead with a comfortable overhand grip.
Keep a small, steady bend in the elbows and pull the bar in an arc toward the thighs by moving at the shoulders.
Return the arms overhead under control, maintaining the same elbow angle and keeping the torso supported.
baseInstructions: Face a high cable pulley fitted with a straight bar. Grasp it with a comfortable overhand grip, step back and keep the elbows softly extended.
Move at the shoulders to draw the bar toward the thighs, keeping the elbow angle and torso steady.
Return the arms overhead under control without letting the weight pull the back into an arch.

candidates.variation: Kneeling with head / upper arms supported on bench
candidates.rationale: Both use a cable to extend the elbows with the upper arms held near the head. The kneeling version adds bench support and a high-pulley bar instead of the standing low-pulley rope.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Bench support, cable direction and arm orientation must remain clear if treated as a setup option.
candidates.name: Kneeling Cable Triceps Extension
instructions: Place a bench sideways in front of a high pulley machine.
Hold a straight bar attachment above your head with your hands about 6 inches apart with your palms facing down.
Face away from the machine and kneel.
Place your head and the back of your upper arms on the bench. Your elbows should be bent with the forearms pointing towards the high pulley. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your upper arms close to your head at all times with the elbows in, press the bar out in a semicircular motion until the elbows are locked and your arms are parallel to the floor. Contract the triceps hard and keep this position for a second. Exhale as you perform this movement.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Attach a rope to the bottom pulley of the pulley machine.

Grasping the rope with both hands, extend your arms with your hands directly above your head using a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Your elbows should be in close to your head and the arms should be perpendicular to the floor with the knuckles aimed at the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower the rope behind your head as you hold the upper arms stationary. Inhale as you perform this movement and pause when your triceps are fully stretched.
Return to the starting position by flexing your triceps as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: The candidate holds the legs nearly vertical and reaches the hands toward the toes while curling the torso; the base curls the shoulders with bent knees and grounded feet. The core repetition remains a short trunk curl.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Vertical legs and reaching arms change leverage; keep as an optional crunch setup rather than deleting the cue.
candidates.name: Toe Touchers
instructions: To begin, lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed against the floor. Your arms should be lying across your sides with the palms facing down.

Your legs should be touching each other. Slowly elevate your legs up in the air until they are almost perpendicular to the floor with a slight bend at the knees. Your feet should be parallel to the floor.
Move your arms so that they are fully extended at a 45 degree angle from the floor. This is the starting position.
While keeping your lower back pressed against the floor, slowly lift your torso and use your hands to try and touch your toes. Remember to exhale while perform this part of the exercise.
Slowly begin to lower your torso and arms back down to the starting position while inhaling. Remember to keep your arms straight out pointing towards your toes.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both use a small rotational crunch bringing one shoulder toward the opposite knee. The candidate crosses one leg over the other on the floor; the base supports the lower legs on a bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Broaden the surviving setup to allow floor or supported legs; do not require elbow-to-knee contact.
candidates.name: Elbow to Knee
instructions: Lie on the floor, crossing your right leg across your bent left knee. Clasp your hands behind your head, beginning with your shoulder blades on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Perform the motion by flexing the spine and rotating your torso to bring the left elbow to the right knee.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with the lower legs supported on a bench and knees bent. Rest the fingertips lightly beside the head.
Curl one shoulder toward the opposite knee without pulling the neck or requiring elbow-to-knee contact.
Lower under control and complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: Both are a small shoulder curl with a steady lower back. The candidate holds the legs bent in tabletop and crosses the ankles instead of planting the feet.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Elevated legs change leverage and support demands; preserve as an optional setup.
candidates.name: Tuck Crunch
instructions: Lie on the back and cross the ankles, with thighs pointing upward and knees bent to about a right angle so the shins are roughly parallel to the floor. Cross the arms over the chest.
Keep the lower back steady and curl the shoulders a small distance from the floor.
Lower under control and repeat without swinging the legs.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both are seated, platform-loaded calf presses with knees softly extended and held still while the ankles raise and lower the heels. The longer title specifies a leg-press machine.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Machine-specific safeties and foot-platform security; distinguish from bent-knee Seated Calf Raise.
candidates.name: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine
instructions: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance.
Place the balls of both feet securely on the leg-press platform with the heels free and knees softly extended. Use a comfortable neutral toe position.

Press on the platform by raising your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Adjust the seat so that your legs are only slightly bent in the start position. The balls of your feet should be firmly on the platform.
Select an appropriate weight, and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position.

Straighten the legs by extending the knees, just barely lifting the weight from the stack. Your ankle should be fully flexed, toes pointing up. Execute the movement by pressing downward through the balls of your feet as far as possible.
After a brief pause, reverse the motion and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both sit at a row machine and pull handles from chest level toward the torso. The iso instructions still use both hands; they do not describe a separate unilateral repetition.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Confirm the specific machine supports the chest, as the generic base assumes; retain plate-loading and handle adjustments.
candidates.name: Leverage Iso Row
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level. Grasp the handles with a neutral grip with both hands. This will be your starting position.
Pull the handles towards your torso, retracting your shoulder blades as you flex the elbow.

Pause at the bottom of the motion, and then slowly return the handles to the starting position. For multiple repetitions, avoid completely returning the weight to the stops to keep tension on the muscles being worked.
baseInstructions: Adjust the machine so the handles are reachable with the chest supported.
Pull the handles toward the ribs and return slowly without lifting off the pad.

candidates.rationale: Both bring two handles together in front of the chest with a steady soft elbow bend. The variant specifies low pulleys and an upward arc from below the waist.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Pulley height and line of pull meaningfully change the emphasis; preserve them as form options if the library uses one crossover entry.
candidates.name: Low Cable Crossover
instructions: To move into the starting position, place the pulleys at the low position, select the resistance to be used and grasp a handle in each hand.
Step forward, gaining tension in the pulleys. Your palms should be facing forward, hands below the waist, and your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
With a slight bend in your arms, draw your hands upward and toward the midline of your body. Your hands should come together in front of your chest, palms facing up.
Return your arms back to the starting position after a brief pause.
baseInstructions: Stand between cable handles with a stable staggered stance and softly bent elbows.
Bring the hands together in front of the chest, then reopen without forcing the shoulders behind you.

candidates.variation: Lying on floor instead of standing
candidates.rationale: Both keep the elbows by the torso and curl a low-pulley bar with an underhand grip. The floor version changes body support while retaining the same elbow movement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Body support and cable distance differ; retain a supported setup note rather than using the lying image for standing instructions.
candidates.name: Lying Cable Curl
instructions: Grab a straight bar or E-Z bar attachment that is attached to the low pulley with both hands, using an underhand (palms facing up) shoulder-width grip.
Lie flat on your back on top of an exercise mat in front of the weight stack with your feet flat against the frame of the pulley machine and your legs straight.
With your arms extended and your elbows close to your body slightly bend your arms. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your upper arms stationary and the elbows close to your body, curl the bar up slowly toward your chest as you breathe out and you squeeze the biceps.
After a second squeeze at the top of the movement, slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both sit upright at a low pulley using a rope, keep the upper arms horizontal, and row with elbows flared. One pulls below the neck and the other brings the hands closer to the ears.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain the high-elbow rear-delt row cue and a comfortable endpoint; distinct from an elbows-tucked lower-rib cable row.
candidates.name: Low Pulley Row To Neck
instructions: Sit on a low pulley row machine with a rope attachment.

Grab the ends of the rope using a palms-down grip and sit with your back straight and your knees slightly bent. Tip: Keep your back almost completely vertical and your arms fully extended in front of you. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your torso stationary, lift your elbows and start bending them as you pull the rope towards your neck while exhaling. Throughout the movement your upper arms should remain parallel to the floor. Tip: Continue this motion until your hands are almost next to your ears (the forearms will not be parallel to the floor at the end of the movement as they will be angled a bit upwards) and your elbows are out away from your sides.
After holding for a second or so at the contracted position, come back slowly to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Again, during no part of the movement should the torso move.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit on a stable bench facing a low cable pulley with a rope attachment, keeping enough distance for the arms to extend.
Attach a rope to the pulley and grasp it with an overhand grip. Your arms should be extended and parallel to the floor with the elbows flared out.
Keep your lower back upright and slide your hips back so that your knees are slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Pull the cable attachment towards your upper chest, just below the neck, as you keep your elbows up and out to the sides. Continue this motion as you exhale until the elbows travel slightly behind the back. Tip: Keep your upper arms horizontal, perpendicular to the torso and parallel to the floor throughout the motion.
Go back to the initial position where the arms are extended and the shoulders are stretched forward. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both squat with a bar on the upper back. The candidate specifies a high trap position, upright torso, hip-width stance and very deep descent.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: High-bar placement and depth can be style cues without requiring every user to adopt them.
candidates.name: Olympic Squat
instructions: Begin with a barbell supported on top of the traps. The chest should be up, and the head facing forward. Adopt a hip width stance with the feet turned out as needed.

Descend by flexing the knees, refraining from moving the hips back as much as possible. This requires that the knees travel forward; ensure that they stay aligned with the feet. The goal is to keep the torso as upright as possible. Continue all the way down, keeping the weight on the front of the heel.
At the moment the upper legs contact the lower, reverse the motion, driving the weight upward.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.variation: Outward curl path and inner-biceps label
candidates.rationale: Both perform dumbbell curls on an incline bench. The candidate turns the forearms outward and finishes beside the shoulders rather than directly in front.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Different upper-arm/forearm orientation, not a separately isolated inner muscle.
candidates.name: Incline Inner Biceps Curl
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench.
The dumbbells should be at arm's length hanging at your sides and your palms should be facing out. This will be your starting position.

Now as you exhale curl the weight outward and up while keeping your forearms in line with your side deltoids. Continue the curl until the dumbbells are at shoulder height and to the sides of your deltoids. Tip: The end of the movement should look similar to a double biceps pose.
After a second contraction at the top of the movement, start to inhale and slowly lower the weights back to the starting position using the same path used to bring them up.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand held at arms length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.variation: Outward curl path and inner-biceps label
candidates.rationale: Both stand and curl dumbbells with stationary upper arms. The candidate turns the palms from neutral to upward while curling outward toward the outer deltoids.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional curl path and wrist rotation; avoid treating an inner-biceps label as a distinct movement family.
candidates.name: Standing Inner-Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand up with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso. Your legs should be at about shoulder's width apart from each other.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing inward in a neutral position. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights out while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Your wrist should turn so that when the weights are fully elevated you have supinated grip (palms facing up).
Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Tip: Keep the forearms aligned with your outer deltoids.
Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in. Remember to rotate the wrists as you lower the weight in order to switch back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both sit on a flat bench and curl two dumbbells while rotating from a neutral grip. The candidate directs the forearms outward toward the deltoids.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep seated setup as the retained base; outward arm path is the narrower variation.
candidates.name: Seated Dumbbell Inner Biceps Curl
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing inward in a neutral position. This will be your starting position.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the dumbbells out and up, turning the palms out as you lift and keeping your forearms in line with your outer deltoids. Tips:

Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in. Remember to rotate your arms as you lower the dumbbells so that you can switch back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights and start twisting the wrists once the dumbbells pass your thighs so that the palms of your hands face forward at the end of the movement. Make sure that you contract the biceps as you breathe out and make sure that only the forearms move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in and as you rotate the wrists back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.variation: Overhead assistance bands added to the standard lift
candidates.rationale: The candidate retains the Barbell Bench Press movement and adds overhead assistance bands to the bar or setup. The base supplies the same main movement without that loading accessory.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve changing resistance/assistance, anchor setup and load notation as optional modifiers; bar weight alone is not comparable across setups.
candidates.name: Reverse Band Bench Press
instructions: Secure bands to rated overhead rack anchors and connect them evenly to a barbell above a flat bench. Set the rack safeties before lying down.
Unrack with a controlled grip, lower the bar toward the chest, then press back up while keeping the shoulders supported.
Complete the selected repetitions and rerack securely. Record the bar and plate load; do not subtract an estimated band assistance value.
baseInstructions: Set the bench and rack safeties before lifting. Lie with feet planted, hands slightly wider than shoulders, and shoulder blades supported.
Unrack the bar over the chest. Lower it under control to a comfortable chest-level position.
Press back to the starting position, then return the bar securely to the rack after the set.

candidates.variation: Overhead assistance bands added to the standard lift
candidates.rationale: The candidate retains the Box Squat movement and adds overhead assistance bands to the bar or setup. The base supplies the same main movement without that loading accessory.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve changing resistance/assistance, anchor setup and load notation as optional modifiers; bar weight alone is not comparable across setups.
candidates.name: Reverse Band Box Squat
instructions: Begin in a power rack with a box at the appropriate height behind you. Set up the bands either on band pegs or attached to the top of the rack, ensuring they will be directly above the bar during the squat. Attach the other end to the bar.

Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wider for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, or closer together for more quad development. Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips until you are seated on the box. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Pause when you reach the box, and relax the hip flexors. Never bounce off of a box.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward off of the box as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe. Use care to return the barbell to the rack.
baseInstructions: The box squat allows you to squat to desired depth and develop explosive strength in the squat movement. Begin in a power rack with a box at the appropriate height behind you. Typically, you would aim for a box height that brings you to a parallel squat, but you can train higher or lower if desired.

Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wider for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings, or closer together for more quad development. Keep your head facing forward.

With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips until you are seated on the box. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Pause when you reach the box, and relax the hip flexors. Never bounce off of a box.
Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward off of the box as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe.

candidates.variation: Overhead assistance bands added to the standard lift
candidates.rationale: The candidate retains the Barbell Deadlift movement and adds overhead assistance bands to the bar or setup. The base supplies the same main movement without that loading accessory.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve changing resistance/assistance, anchor setup and load notation as optional modifiers; bar weight alone is not comparable across setups.
candidates.name: Reverse Band Deadlift
instructions: Attach bands evenly from rated overhead anchors to a barbell on the floor. Stand with the bar close and take a balanced grip.
Brace the trunk and extend the hips and knees to stand tall without arching backward or forcing the shoulders together.
Hinge and bend the knees to lower the bar under control to the floor, then reset before repeating.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.

candidates.variation: Overhead assistance bands added to the standard lift
candidates.rationale: The candidate retains the Sumo Deadlift movement and adds overhead assistance bands to the bar or setup. The base supplies the same main movement without that loading accessory.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve changing resistance/assistance, anchor setup and load notation as optional modifiers; bar weight alone is not comparable across setups.
candidates.name: Reverse Band Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Begin with a bar loaded on the floor inside of a power rack. Attach bands to the top of the rack, using either pegs or the frame itself. Attach the other end to the barbell.

Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide, near the collars. Bend at the hips to grip the bar. The arms should be directly below the shoulders, inside the legs, and you can use a pronated grip, a mixed grip, or hook grip. Relax the shoulders, which in effect lengthens your arms.

Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the back half of your feet. Extend through the hips and knees.
As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Return the weight to the ground by bending at the hips and controlling the weight on the way down.
baseInstructions: Take a wide stance with toes turned out and grip the bar inside the knees.
Brace and push the floor away to stand, then lower with the bar close to the body.

candidates.variation: Overhead assistance bands and power-squat style added to the standard lift
candidates.rationale: The candidate retains the Barbell Squat movement and adds overhead assistance bands and power-squat style to the bar or setup. The base supplies the same main movement without that loading accessory.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve changing resistance/assistance, anchor setup and load notation as optional modifiers; bar weight alone is not comparable across setups.
candidates.name: Reverse Band Power Squat
instructions: Begin in a power rack with the pins and bar set at the appropriate height. After loading the bar, attach bands to the top of the rack, using either pegs or the frame itself. Attach the other end of the bands to the bar.

Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wide for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings.

Keep your head facing forward. With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips as much as possible. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Lower bar position necessitates a greater torso lean to keep the bar over the heels. Continue until you break parallel, which is defined as the crease of the hip being in line with the top of the knee.

Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe, until you have returned to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Set the rack safeties and place the bar securely across the upper back.
Brace, bend the hips and knees to a comfortable depth, and stand by pressing through the whole foot.

candidates.rationale: Both perform an anchored-feet sit-up from bent knees. The candidate reverses after only three-quarters of the lowering instead of returning fully.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Partial lowering is a range/tempo option, not a mandatory standard sit-up instruction.
candidates.name: 3/4 Sit-Up
instructions: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees.
At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on the back with knees bent and feet secured under a suitable fixed foot anchor. Cross the arms over the chest or rest the fingertips lightly beside the head without pulling the neck.
Raise the torso in a controlled sit-up without throwing the arms forward.
Lower slowly and repeat the selected repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both lie on an incline bench under a Smith bar and press above the upper chest. The partial version repeats only the short upper portion with slightly bent elbows.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Partial reps are a programming/form option, not evidence that the standard full-range instructions should be shortened.
candidates.name: Smith Incline Partial Press
instructions: Place an incline bench beneath a Smith-machine bar and set the safeties. Lie back with a shoulder-width overhand grip and the bar above the upper chest with elbows slightly bent.
Extend the elbows through this short upper portion of the press while keeping the shoulders supported.
Lower only to the initial slight elbow bend, repeat under control and engage the hooks securely after the set.
baseInstructions: Place an incline bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down and your arms are almost fully extended. Once the weight you need is selected, lie down on the incline bench and make sure your upper chest is aligned with the barbell. Using a pronated grip (palms facing forward) that is wider than shoulder width, unlock the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your upper chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

candidates.variation: Slightly outward strict kettlebell press path
candidates.rationale: Both current descriptions clean one bell to the shoulder and strictly press overhead without leg drive or leaning. The candidate starts palm-in and describes a slightly outward path; Para Press starts palm-forward.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Consider simplifying the retained name to Single-Arm Kettlebell Press; preserve the comfortable grip/path option.
candidates.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Military Press To The Side
instructions: Clean one kettlebell to the shoulder with the palm facing inward and the elbow supported near the torso.
Brace the trunk and press the kettlebell overhead along a slightly outward path without leg drive or leaning back.
Lower under control to the rack and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Clean one kettlebell to the shoulder and rotate the palm to face forward while keeping the wrist controlled.
Brace the trunk and press the kettlebell overhead without using the legs or leaning back.
Lower under control to the shoulder rack and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.

candidates.rationale: Both curl the pelvis backward to lift the hips from the floor. The candidate starts the bent legs only two inches off the floor and draws them farther toward the chest; the base starts with hips and knees near right angles.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve the lower-leg start as a harder optional range, while keeping the controlled pelvic curl central.
candidates.name: Low-Start Reverse Crunch
instructions: Lay flat on the floor with your arms next to your sides.
Now bend your knees at around a 75 degree angle and lift your feet off the floor by around 2 inches.

Using your lower abs, bring your knees in towards you as you maintain the 75 degree angle bend in your legs. Continue this movement until you raise your hips off of the floor by rolling your pelvis backward. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: At the end of the movement your knees will be over your chest.
Squeeze your abs at the top of the movement for a second and then return to the starting position slowly as you breathe in. Tip: Maintain a controlled motion at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on the back with hips and knees bent near right angles and arms resting by the sides.
Use a small controlled pelvic curl to lift the hips slightly from the floor without swinging the legs or forcing the knees to the chest.
Lower the pelvis under control and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both lean back with grounded heels and straight arms, then row the chest toward the hands. The candidate uses suspension-trainer handles; the base uses rings.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Broaden the surviving name and equipment to Suspension Row if consolidating; keep rated anchors and adjustable body angle.
candidates.name: Inverted Row with Straps
instructions: Secure a suspension trainer to a suitable rated anchor. Grasp both handles and lean back with your heels grounded, body straight and arms extended.
Begin by flexing the elbow, pulling your chest to your hands. Retract your shoulder blades as you perform the movement.
Pause at the top of the motion, and return yourself to the start position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Set secure rings to an appropriate height and lean back with straight arms.
Pull the chest toward the hands, then lower slowly; a more upright body angle makes the exercise easier.

candidates.variation: Tall flat bench instead of preacher-bench support
candidates.rationale: Both are prone/chest-supported barbell curls with hanging arms and still upper arms. The candidate requires a tall flat bench rather than a preacher support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Bar clearance and shoulder angle depend on the support.
candidates.name: Lying High Bench Barbell Curl
instructions: Lie face forward on a tall flat bench while holding a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing up). Tip: If you are holding a barbell grab it using a shoulder-width grip and if you are using an E-Z Bar grab it on the inner handles. Your upper body should be positioned in a way that the upper chest is over the end of the bench and the barbell is hanging in front of you with the arms extended and perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the elbows in and the upper arms stationary, curl the weight up in a semi-circular motion as you contract the biceps and exhale. Hold at the top of the movement for a second.
As you inhale, slowly go back to the starting position. Tip: Maintain full control of the weight at all times and avoid any swinging. Remember, only the forearms should move throughout the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lean chest down against the preacher bench support and take a straight barbell from secure reachable rests or a controlled handoff. Let the arms hang with a comfortable underhand grip.
Curl the bar while keeping the upper arms still and the chest supported.
Lower under control and return the bar to its support after the selected repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both support the body on parallel bars, bend the elbows, and press back up. Chest Dip adds a slight forward lean; Tricep Dip specifies an upright torso.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Rename the survivor to Parallel-Bar Dip and allow controlled torso angle; preserve chest/triceps involvement rather than promising isolation.
candidates.name: Chest Dip
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with shoulders held down.
Lean slightly forward, lower through a comfortable elbow bend, and press back up without bouncing at the bottom.
baseInstructions: Support the body on parallel bars with an upright torso.
Bend the elbows through a comfortable depth, then press back to support without shrugging or bouncing.

candidates.variation: Upper arms held behind the head
candidates.rationale: Both lie on a bench and extend the elbows with upper arms fixed. The candidate holds the upper arms back nearly parallel to the bench instead of pointing above the chest.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This meaningfully changes shoulder position and stretch; preserve it as an optional extension angle.
candidates.name: Lying Barbell Triceps Extension Behind the Head
instructions: While holding a barbell or EZ Curl bar with a pronated grip (palms facing forward), lie on your back on a flat bench with your head close to the end of the bench. Tip: If you are holding a barbell grab it using a shoulder-width grip and if you are using an E-Z Bar grab it on the inner handles.

Extend your arms in front of you and slowly bring the bar back in a semi circular motion (while keeping the arms extended) to a position over your head. At the end of this step your arms should be overhead and parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position. Tip: Keep your elbows in at all times.
As you inhale, lower the bar by bending at the elbows and while keeping the upper arm stationary. Keep lowering the bar until your forearms are perpendicular to the floor.

As you exhale bring the bar back up to the starting position by pushing the bar up in a semi-circular motion until the lower arms are also parallel to the floor. Contract the triceps hard at the top of the movement for a second. Tip: Again, only the forearms should move. The upper arms should remain stationary at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on a bench with a light bar above the chest.
Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward a comfortable point near the forehead, then extend the elbows without letting the shoulders drift.

candidates.rationale: Both row dumbbells with the chest supported on an incline bench. The candidate flares the elbows into a T while the base rows toward the sides.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Elbow path changes emphasis toward upper back/rear delts; preserve it as an optional cue.
candidates.name: Wide-Elbow Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
instructions: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and lie face down on an incline bench that is set to an incline that is approximately 30 degrees.
Let the arms hang to your sides fully extended as they point to the floor.
Turn the wrists until your hands have a pronated (palms down) grip.
Now flare the elbows out. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, start to pull the dumbbells up as if you are doing a reverse bench press. You will do this by bending at the elbows and bringing the upper arms up as you let the forearms hang. Continue this motion until the upper arms are at the same level as your back. Tip: The elbows will come out to the side and your upper arms and torso should make the letter "T" at the top of the movement. Hold the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly go back down to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.

candidates.rationale: Both hinge and row a barbell. The candidate flares the elbows and pulls toward the upper chest rather than the lower ribs.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Upper-back/rear-delt emphasis and comfortable shoulder range; this is more than a name-only duplicate.
candidates.name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a barbell using a wide (higher than shoulder width) and overhand (palms facing your body) grip.

Bend knees slightly and bend over as you keep the natural arch of your back. Let the arms hang in front of you as they hold the bar. Once your torso is parallel to the floor, flare the elbows out and away from your body. Tip: Your torso and your arms should resemble the letter "T". Now you are ready to begin the exercise.

While keeping the upper arms perpendicular to the torso, pull the barbell up towards your upper chest as you squeeze the rear delts and you breathe out. Tip: When performed correctly, this exercise should resemble a bench press in reverse. Also, refrain from using your biceps to do the work. Focus on targeting the rear delts; the arms should only act as hooks.
Slowly go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Hinge at the hips with knees softly bent and a steady trunk.
Pull the bar toward the lower ribs, pause, and lower without jerking the torso upward.

candidates.rationale: The candidate uses a wide stance and nearly straight legs for repeated barbell hip hinges; after the first lift it need not touch the floor. The retained Romanian Deadlift covers the same repeated hinge pattern with a soft knee bend.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Wide stance and initial floor pickup need explicit optional cues; keep the knees soft.
candidates.name: Wide Stance Stiff Legs
instructions: Begin with a barbell loaded on the floor. Adopt a wide stance, and then bend at the hips to grab the bar. Your hips should be as far back as possible, and your legs nearly straight. Keep your back straight, and your head and chest up. This will be your starting position.

Begin the movement be engaging the hips, driving them forward as you allow the arms to hang straight. Continue until you are standing straight up, and then slowly return the weight to the starting position. For successive reps, the weight need not touch the floor.
baseInstructions: Hold the bar near the thighs with knees softly bent.
Push the hips back while keeping the bar close, then drive the hips forward to stand before the back begins to round.

candidates.rationale: Both bend and extend the elbows in a hands-behind bench dip. The candidate raises the heels onto a second bench and places a dumbbell on the lap.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: External load, assisted loading/unloading, and raised-foot setup must remain explicit and loggable.
candidates.name: Weighted Bench Dip
instructions: Place one bench behind the body for the hands and another ahead for the heels. Support the body with arms extended and have a partner place a dumbbell securely on the lap.
Bend the elbows to lower through a comfortable controlled range, then press back up while keeping the benches stable.
After the selected repetitions, have the partner remove the dumbbell before moving the legs off the forward bench and dismounting.
baseInstructions: For this exercise you will need to place a bench behind your back. With the bench perpendicular to your body, and while looking away from it, hold on to the bench on its edge with the hands fully extended, separated at shoulder width. The legs will be extended forward, bent at the waist and perpendicular to your torso. This will be your starting position.

Slowly lower your body as you inhale by bending at the elbows until you lower yourself far enough to where there is an angle slightly smaller than 90 degrees between the upper arm and the forearm. Tip: Keep the elbows as close as possible throughout the movement. Forearms should always be pointing down.
Using your triceps to bring your torso up again, lift yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both stand between low cables and press from shoulder height to overhead. One presses each arm in turn while the base presses both together.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Per-side repetition counting and unilateral timing must be preserved if merged.
candidates.name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight.
Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press one side directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight.
Stand directly in between the uprights. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press the handles directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat.

candidates.variation: Alternating arm while other arm holds
candidates.rationale: Both bring cable handles to the body midline with softly bent elbows. The variant holds one hand forward while moving the other arm and alternates sides.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The stationary-arm hold and per-side repetition convention need an explicit mode; do not silently replace bilateral guidance.
candidates.name: Single-Arm Cable Crossover
instructions: Begin by moving the pulleys to the high position, select the resistance to be used, and take a handle in each hand.

Step forward in front of both pulleys with your arms extended in front of you, bringing your hands together. Your head and chest should be up as you lean forward, while your feet should be staggered. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your left arm in place, allow your right arm to extend out to the side, maintaining a slight bend at the elbow. The right arm should be perpendicular to the body at approximately shoulder level.
Return your arm back to the starting position by pulling your hand back to the midline of the body.
Hold for a second at the starting position and repeat the movement on the opposite side. Continue alternating back and forth for the prescribed number of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand between cable handles with a stable staggered stance and softly bent elbows.
Bring the hands together in front of the chest, then reopen without forcing the shoulders behind you.

candidates.rationale: Both are standing dumbbell curls. This version combines a neutral grip with alternating arms instead of curling both together.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep neutral grip, arm path and per-side counting as explicit options if merged. The proposal maps directly to Dumbbell Bicep Curl so the survivor is not also scheduled for consolidation.
candidates.name: Alternate Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
Count one movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both are supinating dumbbell curls while supported on an incline bench. The candidate alternates the arms; the base curls both together.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Optional alternation and consistent repetition convention.
candidates.name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. As you do so, rotate the hand so that the palm is facing up. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbell back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
Count one movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand held at arms length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both raise dumbbells forward from the thighs to approximately shoulder height with a still torso; only the arm order changes.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Offer alternating reps without creating another exercise; preserve the selected counting convention.
candidates.name: Alternating Dumbbell Front Raise
instructions: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells on front of your thighs at arms length with the palms of the hand facing your thighs. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the left dumbbell to the front with a slight bend on the elbow and the palms of the hands always facing down. Continue to go up until you arm is slightly above parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this portion of the movement and pause for a second at the top. Inhale after the second pause.
Now lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position as you simultaneously lift the right dumbbell.
Continue alternating in this fashion until all of the recommended amount of repetitions have been performed for each arm.
baseInstructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of the thighs, with the trunk steady.
Raise both arms together in front to about shoulder height, then lower slowly without leaning back.

candidates.rationale: Both stand with dumbbells at the shoulders and press without leg drive or trunk lean. The candidate holds one arm at the shoulder while pressing the other.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Alternation is optional; define whether logged reps apply per side.
candidates.name: Standing Alternating Dumbbell Press
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand. Raise the dumbbells to your shoulders with your palms facing forward and your elbows pointed out. This will be your starting position.
Extend one arm to press the dumbbell straight up, keeping your off hand in place. Do not lean or jerk the weight during the movement.
After a brief pause, return the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the opposite side, continuing to alternate between arms.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold the dumbbells beside the shoulders, with wrists stacked over elbows.
Press both dumbbells overhead without arching the back, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both clean two kettlebells from a hanging position to the shoulders. The candidate cleans one at a time while holding the other down.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Alternating timing and per-side count, versus two bells moving together.
candidates.name: Alternating Hang Clean
instructions: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.

Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder and hold on to the other kettlebell in a hanging position. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so.
Lower the cleaned kettlebell to a hanging position and clean the alternate kettlebell. Repeat.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
Lower the kettlebells back to the starting position and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both start two kettlebells at the shoulders and strictly press them overhead. The candidate alternates the arms, keeping the other bell racked.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Per-side count and alternating work/rest; the bilateral base remains distinct from a single-bell press.
candidates.name: Alternating Kettlebell Press
instructions: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
Press one directly overhead by extending through the elbow, turning it so the palm faces forward while holding the other kettlebell stationary .
Lower the pressed kettlebell to the starting position and immediately press with your other arm.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Clean two kettlebells to the shoulder rack with palms facing forward and the trunk braced.
Press both bells overhead without leg drive or leaning back, finishing with the arms aligned over the torso.
Lower under control to the shoulder rack and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both hinge and row two kettlebells toward the torso. The candidate moves one bell at a time while the other remains down.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Alternating timing and per-side repetition convention.
candidates.name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
instructions: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and push your butt out as much as possible. As you bend over to get into the starting position grab both kettlebells by the handles.

Pull one kettlebell off of the floor while holding on to the other kettlebell. Retract the shoulder blade of the working side, as you flex the elbow, drawing the kettlebell towards your stomach or rib cage.
Lower the kettlebell in the working arm and repeat with your other arm.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and then push your butt out as much as possible as you bend over to get in the starting position.
Grab both kettlebells and pull them to your stomach, retracting your shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Keep your back straight. Lower and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both press a kettlebell upward from the floor with the upper arm supported at the bottom. The candidate alternates between two bells while the other arm remains extended.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Second bell is held isometrically overhead; retain that optional setup and per-arm count.
candidates.name: Alternating Kettlebell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.
Position one in place on your chest and then the other, gripping the kettlebells on the handle with the palms facing forward.
Extend both arms, so that the kettlebells are being held above your chest. Lower one kettlebell, bringing it to your chest and turn the wrist in the direction of the locked out kettlebell.
Raise the kettlebell and repeat on the opposite side.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Lie on the floor holding a kettlebell with one hand, with your upper arm supported by the floor. The palm should be facing in.
Press the kettlebell straight up toward the ceiling, rotating your wrist.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and repeat.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.

candidates.rationale: Both clean a barbell and receive it in a front squat. The candidate starts on raised boxes and resets on them rather than lifting from the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Block height and reduced first pull are meaningful technical details.
candidates.name: Clean from Blocks
instructions: With a barbell on boxes or stands of the desired height, take an overhand or hook grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight with the elbows pointed out.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the receiving position by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. Aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position. Return the weight to the boxes for the next rep.
baseInstructions: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand (or hook) grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.

candidates.rationale: Both are barbell power cleans received above a full squat. The candidate starts and resets on blocks rather than the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep power catch distinct from full clean; preserve block height and start position.
candidates.name: Power Clean from Blocks
instructions: With a barbell on boxes of the desired height, take a grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips.

In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight. At the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, pull yourself under the bar far enough that it can be racked onto the shoulders, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed.

Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position, and complete the repetition by returning the weight to the boxes.
baseInstructions: Start with the bar over the middle of the feet, hands outside the legs and the trunk braced.
Extend the legs and hips to accelerate the bar close to the body.
Move underneath it and receive it on the front shoulders in a partial squat, with the hips remaining above knee height.
Stand tall and stabilize the front rack, then lower the bar under control using your practiced lifting technique.
Receive the bar in a partial squat with the hips above knee level, then stand to finish the power clean.

candidates.rationale: Both receive a snatch in a partial squat above parallel. The candidate starts on blocks instead of the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Block height and shortened first pull; do not collapse power snatch into full snatch.
candidates.name: Power Snatch from Blocks
instructions: Place a loaded barbell on stable lifting blocks. Take a wide snatch grip, bend the hips and knees and keep the bar close.
Extend the hips and knees to accelerate the bar, then move underneath it as the arms extend overhead.
Receive the bar in a partial squat above parallel. Stand, then lower the bar carefully onto the blocks before the next repetition.
baseInstructions: Begin with a loaded barbell on the floor. The bar should be close to or touching the shins, and a wide grip should be taken on the bar. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar. This will be the starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar from the ground. The back angle should stay the same until the bar passes the knees.

Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, a slightly wider position, pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. The bar should be received in a partial squat. Continue raising the bar to the overhead position, receiving the bar locked out overhead.
Return to a standing position with the weight over head.

candidates.rationale: Both receive the barbell overhead in a squat. The candidate starts and resets on blocks rather than the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Block height and practiced pull segment; keep full-squat catch.
candidates.name: Snatch from Blocks
instructions: Begin with a loaded barbell on boxes or stands of the desired height. A wide grip should be taken on the bar. The feet should be directly below the hips, with the feet turned out as needed. Lower the hips, with the chest up and the head looking forward. The shoulders should be just in front of the bar, with the elbows pointed out. This will be the starting position.
Begin the first pull by driving through the front of the heels, raising the bar from the boxes.

Transition into the second pull by extending through the hips knees and ankles, driving the bar up as quickly as possible. The bar should be close to the body. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. The feet should move to just outside the hips, turned out as necessary. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Keeping the bar aligned over the front of the heels, your head and chest up, drive through heels of the feet to move to a standing position. Carefully return the weight to the boxes.
baseInstructions: Use a technique load in a clear lifting area. Take a wide overhand grip on the bar with feet under the hips and the trunk braced.
Push through the legs and extend the hips to accelerate the bar close to the body.
Move underneath the bar into an overhead squat, receiving it with extended arms and a balanced stance.
Stand from the squat while keeping the bar stable overhead, then lower using your practiced weightlifting technique.
Receive the bar overhead in a squat before standing under control; the partial-squat power snatch is a separate exercise.

candidates.rationale: Both lie on a flat bench and press a barbell. The candidate stops the descent on boards placed over the chest, deliberately reducing range.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Range restriction and board height materially affect load comparisons; this is not a simple alias.
candidates.name: Board Press
instructions: Begin by lying on the bench, getting your head beyond the bar if possible. One to five boards, made out of 2x6's, can be screwed together and held in place by a training partner, bands, or just tucked under your shirt.

Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement.
