You can take a standard bench grip, or shoulder width to focus on the triceps. Pull the bar out of the rack without protracting your shoulders. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart.
Lower the bar to the boards, and then drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.
baseInstructions: Set the bench and rack safeties before lifting. Lie with feet planted, hands slightly wider than shoulders, and shoulder blades supported.
Unrack the bar over the chest. Lower it under control to a comfortable chest-level position.
Press back to the starting position, then return the bar securely to the rack after the set.

candidates.rationale: Both clean a single kettlebell from a hang to the shoulder. The candidate balances it inverted above the fist.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Inverted balance and grip demand materially differ from a normal rack.
candidates.name: Bottoms-Up Clean From The Hang Position
instructions: Stand with a kettlebell held in one hand beside the body. Hinge slightly at the hips and let the bell move back under control.

Extend the hips and guide the bell close to the body into a rack position with its base pointing upward above the fist. Keep the forearm nearly vertical and stop the bell without letting it strike the arm.
Pause briefly while maintaining the inverted balance, then lower under control to the hanging position. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Hold one kettlebell hanging between the legs with the knees softly bent and the hips hinged.
Extend the hips and knees to clean the bell to the shoulder, rotating the hand around the handle as the bell comes close to the body.
Lower to the hanging position under control without placing it on the floor between repetitions. Count each movement on one side as one repetition. Complete the selected repetitions on each side.

candidates.rationale: Both are standing dumbbell curls. This version combines a neutral grip with a cross-body path and alternating sides.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep neutral grip, arm path and per-side counting as explicit options if merged. The proposal maps directly to Dumbbell Bicep Curl so the survivor is not also scheduled for consolidation.
candidates.name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand. Your hands should be down at your side with your palms facing in.

While keeping your palms facing in and without twisting your arm, curl the dumbbell of the right arm up towards your left shoulder as you exhale. Touch the top of the dumbbell to your shoulder and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path as you inhale and then repeat the same movement for the left arm.
Continue alternating in this fashion until the recommended amount of repetitions is performed for each arm.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.variation: Dead-start bench press from rack pins
candidates.rationale: Both press a barbell while lying on a bench. The candidate starts each rep from pins and deliberately removes or limits the initial lowering phase.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Dead-start and selected pin height are meaningful training differences.
candidates.name: Pin Presses
instructions: Pin presses remove the eccentric phase of the bench press, developing starting strength. They also allow you to train a desired range of motion.

The bench should be set up in a power rack. Set the pins to the desired point in your range of motion, whether it just be lockout or an inch off of your chest. The bar should be moved to the pins and prepared for lifting.

Begin by lying on the bench, with the bar directly above the contact point during your regular bench. Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement.
You can take a standard bench grip, or shoulder width to focus on the triceps. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart.
Drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.
Return the bar to the pins, pausing before beginning the next repetition.
baseInstructions: Set the bench and rack safeties before lifting. Lie with feet planted, hands slightly wider than shoulders, and shoulder blades supported.
Unrack the bar over the chest. Lower it under control to a comfortable chest-level position.
Press back to the starting position, then return the bar securely to the rack after the set.

candidates.rationale: Both hinge with a bar on the upper back. The candidate begins bent over under rack pins and extends upward before lowering back to the pins.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Dead-start strength and pin height; preserve the altered repetition start.
candidates.name: Good Morning off Pins
instructions: Begin with a bar on a rack at about the same height as your stomach. Bend over underneath the bar and rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your shoulders. At the proper height, you should be near parallel to the floor when bent over. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Begin the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings, and you are standing with the weight. Slowly lower the weight back to the pins returning to the starting position.
baseInstructions: Begin with a bar on a rack at shoulder height. Rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your shoulders. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Step back from the rack.
Begin by bending at the hips, moving them back as you bend over to near parallel. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Reverse the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings. Continue until you have returned to the starting position.

candidates.variation: Decline bench and starting leg position
candidates.rationale: Both roll the pelvis backward to lift the hips. The candidate grips a decline bench and starts with legs extended nearly parallel to the floor; the base starts supine with bent knees.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Both resistance angle and lever length change. Merge only if those progressions become explicit form options.
candidates.name: Decline Reverse Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back on a decline bench and hold on to the top of the bench with both hands. Don't let your body slip down from this position.

Hold your legs parallel to the floor using your abs to hold them there while keeping your knees and feet together. Tip: Your legs should be fully extended with a slight bend on the knee. This will be your starting position.
While exhaling, move your legs towards the torso as you roll your pelvis backwards and you raise your hips off the bench. At the end of this movement your knees will be touching your chest.
Hold the contraction for a second and move your legs back to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on the back with hips and knees bent near right angles and arms resting by the sides.
Use a small controlled pelvic curl to lift the hips slightly from the floor without swinging the legs or forcing the knees to the chest.
Lower the pelvis under control and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both lift the shoulders a few inches while keeping the lower back supported. The candidate secures the legs on a decline bench, whereas the base lies on the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The angle changes loading and anchoring; keep separate if bench angle is an intentional exercise distinction.
candidates.name: Decline Crunch
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down.
Now place your hands lightly on either side of your head keeping your elbows in. Tip: Don't lock your fingers behind your head.
While pushing the small of your back down in the bench to better isolate your abdominal muscles, begin to roll your shoulders off it.

Continue to push down as hard as you can with your lower back as you contract your abdominals and exhale. Your shoulders should come up off the bench only about four inches, and your lower back should remain on the bench. At the top of the movement, contract your abdominals hard and keep the contraction for a second. Tip: Focus on slow, controlled movement - don't cheat yourself by using momentum.
After the one second contraction, begin to come down slowly again to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Curl the shoulder blades slightly up while keeping the neck relaxed, then lower under control.

candidates.variation: External rotation added to reverse fly
candidates.rationale: Both are incline chest-supported dumbbell reverse flies. The candidate also rotates the upper arms outward during the raise.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The added shoulder-rotation action is a real combination, not just a grip rename; merge only under a broader modifier policy.
candidates.name: Reverse Flyes With External Rotation
instructions: Lie chest down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand and a soft bend in the elbows.
Raise the arms out to the sides and rotate the upper arms outward through a comfortable range as the palms turn inward, without twisting at the wrists.
Lower along the same controlled path and repeat.
baseInstructions: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.variation: Feet elevated for a longer pull
candidates.rationale: Both deadlift a barbell from the floor. The candidate stands on a platform to increase starting range.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Increased range and chosen platform height; more than a wording-only duplicate.
candidates.name: Deficit Deadlift
instructions: Stand on flat, stable weight plates that raise the feet slightly above the floor. Position the bar over the feet and hinge down to grasp it with a shoulder-width grip, using only a height that permits a steady trunk.

With your feet, and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and bend the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back steady, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. After the bar passes the knees, extend the hips to stand tall while keeping the bar close to the body.
Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
baseInstructions: Stand with the bar over the middle of the feet.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip it, brace the trunk, then stand with the bar close to the legs; reverse the movement to lower.

candidates.variation: Flat instead of inclined chest support
candidates.rationale: Both perform a bilateral dumbbell rear-delt fly with the chest supported. The candidate uses a flat bench, whereas the base uses an incline.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support angle changes the load path; keep if meaningful incline/flat choices remain separate.
candidates.name: Flat-Bench Chest-Supported Rear Delt Raise
instructions: Lie chest down on a stable bench with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging below the shoulders.
Keep a soft fixed bend in the elbows and raise both arms outward through a comfortable shoulder range.
Lower both dumbbells slowly. Count one simultaneous raise and return as one repetition; complete the selected total.
baseInstructions: To begin, lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline. Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip).

Extend the arms in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the angle of the bench. The legs should be stationary while applying pressure with the ball of your toes. This is the starting position.

Maintaining the slight bend of the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other (to the side) in an arc motion while exhaling. Tip: Try to squeeze your shoulder blades together to get the best results from this exercise.
The arms should be elevated until they are parallel to the floor.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the weights back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both rotate the torso side to side while leaning back from sitting. Plate Twist adds a plate and lifts/crosses the feet, while the base grounds the heels and already supports optional load.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Lifted feet are a meaningful balance progression and the candidate uses per-side rather than total repetitions; merge only if the product treats those as options.
candidates.name: Plate Twist
instructions: Lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your legs fully extended and your upper body upright. Grab the plate by its sides with both hands out in front of your abdominals with your arms slightly bent.

Slowly cross your legs near your ankles and lift them up off the ground. Your knees should also be bent slightly. Note: Move your upper body back slightly to help keep you balanced turning this exercise. This is the starting position.
Move the plate to the left side and touch the floor with it. Breathe out as you perform that movement.

Come back to the starting position as you breathe in and then repeat the movement but this time to the right side of the body. Tip: Use a slow controlled movement at all times. Jerking motions can injure the back.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Sit with knees bent and heels grounded.
Lean back slightly with the spine long and rotate the chest a little to one side, then the other, keeping the movement controlled.
Count each turn to one side as one repetition; the entered count is the total across both directions.

candidates.rationale: Both perform a barbell hang clean with a front-squat catch. The candidate starts below the knees; the base starts near mid-thigh.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Start height changes the practiced pull segment and should remain selectable if consolidated.
candidates.name: Hang Clean - Below the Knees
instructions: Begin with a shoulder width, double overhand or hook grip, with the bar hanging just below the knees. Your back should be straight and inclined slightly forward.

Begin by aggressively extending through the hips, knees and ankles, driving the weight upward. As you do so, shrug your shoulders towards your ears. As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out.

At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.
baseInstructions: Hold a barbell at mid-thigh with an overhand grip just outside the legs. Bend slightly at the hips and knees, keeping the bar close and the torso steady.
Extend the hips and knees to accelerate the bar, then bend under it as the elbows rotate forward. Receive the bar across the front shoulders in a controlled squat.
Stand with the elbows lifted, then lower the bar to the hanging start under control. Count the clean, stand and controlled return as one repetition.

candidates.rationale: Both perform a barbell hang snatch into an overhead squat. The candidate begins below the knees instead of around the hips.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Different practiced pull segment; preserve start height.
candidates.name: Hang Snatch - Below Knees
instructions: Begin with a wide grip on the bar, with an overhand or hook grip. The feet should be directly below the hips with the feet turned out. Your knees should be slightly bent, and the torso inclined forward. The spine should be fully extended and the head facing forward. The bar should be just below the knees. This will be your starting position.
Aggressively extend through the legs and hips. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Return to a standing position with the weight overhead, and then return the weight to the floor under control.
baseInstructions: Begin with a wide grip on the bar, with an overhand or hook grip. The feet should be directly below the hips with the feet turned out. Your knees should be slightly bent, and the torso inclined forward. The spine should be fully extended and the head facing forward. The bar should be at the hips. This will be your starting position.
Aggressively extend through the legs and hips. At peak extension, shrug the shoulders and allow the elbows to flex to the side.

As you move your feet into the receiving position, forcefully pull yourself below the bar as you elevate the bar overhead. Receive the bar with your body as low as possible and the arms fully extended overhead.
Return to a standing position with the weight overhead. Follow by returning the weight to the ground under control.

candidates.variation: Lying on flat bench rather than standing
candidates.rationale: Both use a fixed soft elbow bend to bring the cable handles together in front of the chest. The flat-bench version lies between low pulleys rather than standing.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The supported body position and resistance line differ. Consolidation would need a selectable supported setup.
candidates.name: Flat Bench Cable Flyes
instructions: Position a flat bench between two low pulleys so that when you are laying on it, your chest will be lined up with the cable pulleys.
Lay flat on the bench and keep your feet on the ground.
Take both handles while seated, then lie back under control. Set the bench distance so the handles can be returned without reaching beyond control.

Extend your arms by your side with a slight bend on your elbows. Tip: You will keep this bend constant through the whole movement. Your arms should be parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

Now start lifting the arms in a semi-circle motion directly in front of you by pulling the cables together until both hands meet at the top of the movement. Squeeze your chest as you perform this motion and breathe out during this movement. Also, hold the contraction for a second at the top. Tip: When performed correctly, at the top position of this movement, your arms should be perpendicular to your torso and the floor touching above your chest.
Slowly come back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand between cable handles with a stable staggered stance and softly bent elbows.
Bring the hands together in front of the chest, then reopen without forcing the shoulders behind you.

candidates.rationale: Both pull on rings, transition the shoulders above the hands, and press to support. The candidate explicitly initiates a leg swing and kip, while the base describes a controlled pull.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Kipping is a distinct skill and movement strategy; consolidate only under a deliberate strict-versus-kipping options policy.
candidates.name: Kipping Ring Muscle-Up
instructions: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings.
Begin with a movement swinging your legs backward slightly.

Counter that movement by swinging your legs forward and up, jerking your chin and chest back, pulling yourself up with both arms as you do so. As you reach the top position of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits as you roll your shoulders forward, allowing your elbows to move straight back behind you. This puts you into the proper position to continue into the dip portion of the movement.
Maintaining control and stability, extend through the elbow to complete the motion.
Use care when lowering yourself to the ground.
Count the pull, transition to support, and controlled return to hanging as one repetition.
baseInstructions: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings. Initiate a pull up by pulling the elbows down to your side, flexing the elbows.

As you reach the top position of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits as you roll your shoulders forward, allowing your elbows to move straight back behind you. This puts you into the proper position to continue into the dip portion of the movement.
Maintaining control and stability, extend through the elbow to complete the motion.
Use care when lowering yourself to the ground.

candidates.variation: Named torso angle and finish position
candidates.rationale: Both use underhand pulling on a bar. The candidate leans substantially backward and pulls the sternum to the bar, unlike the base chin-clearance movement.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: This changes the pull direction and endpoint materially. Preserve as a progression if those distinctions belong in the library.
candidates.name: Gironda Sternum Chins
instructions: Grasp the pull-up bar with a shoulder width underhand grip.
Now hang with your arms fully extended and stick your chest out and lean back. Tip: You will be leaning back throughout the entire movement. This will be your starting position.

Start pulling yourself towards the bar with your spine arched throughout the movement and the neck in a comfortable position as the torso leans back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: At the upper end of the movement, your hips and legs will be at about a 45-degree angle to the floor.

Keep pulling until your collarbone passes the bar and your lower chest or sternum area touches it. Hold that contraction for a second. Tip: By the time you've completed this portion of the movement; your head will be parallel to the floor.
Slowly start going back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Take an underhand grip on a secure bar and begin from a controlled hang.
Pull the elbows toward the ribs to raise the chin, then lower without kicking.

candidates.rationale: Both curl dumbbells with the upper arms supported on a preacher pad. The candidate works one arm at a time rather than both together.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Per-side counting; retaining unilateral entries may be intentional.
candidates.name: One Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench with one upper arm supported on the pad and a dumbbell in that hand.
Curl the dumbbell without lifting the upper arm from the pad.
Extend the elbow to lower the forearm through a comfortable range. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Rest the upper arms fully on the preacher pad.
Curl the dumbbells without lifting the arms from the pad, then extend the elbows through a comfortable range.

candidates.rationale: Both flex the elbows against a low cable, but the preacher version sits with the upper arms supported forward on a pad instead of beside the torso.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Shoulder angle and upper-arm support materially change the curl setup. Keep separate unless the product explicitly treats supported curls as form options.
candidates.name: Cable Preacher Curl
instructions: Place a preacher bench about 2 feet in front of a pulley machine.
Attach a straight bar to the low pulley.
Sit at the preacher bench with the bar within reach. Grasp it before placing the upper arms on the pad, and adjust the bench distance so you can return the handle under control.
Grab the bar and fully extend your arms on top of the preacher bench pad. This will be your starting position.
Now start pulling the weight up towards your shoulders and squeeze the biceps hard at the top of the movement. Exhale as you perform this motion. Also, hold for a second at the top.
Now slowly lower the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both jump onto a box. The candidate immediately drops or jumps back down and repeats; the base steps down and resets.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The rebound landing demand is a substantive plyometric progression. Merge only if jump-down cadence is handled as programming, not as a separate movement.
candidates.name: Box Jump (Multiple Response)
instructions: Assume a relaxed stance facing the box or platform approximately an arm's length away. Arms should be down at the sides and legs slightly bent.
Using the arms to aid in the initial burst, jump upward and forward, landing with feet simultaneously on top of the box or platform.
Immediately drop or jump back down to the original starting place; then repeat the sequence.
baseInstructions: Choose a low stable box and stand close enough for a controlled jump.
Bend the hips and knees, jump onto the box with a quiet balanced landing, then step down before repeating.

candidates.variation: Seated bench posture and trunk movement
candidates.rationale: Both draw the knees toward the torso then extend them. The candidate sits on a bench and brings the torso toward the knees; the base keeps the torso on the floor.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seated versus supine support and the added trunk motion are meaningful. Earlier user preference preserved seated/standing options, so this is conditional only.
candidates.name: Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
instructions: Sit on a bench with the legs stretched out in front of you slightly below parallel and your arms holding on to the sides of the bench. Your torso should be leaning backwards around a 45-degree angle from the bench. This will be your starting position.
Bring the knees in toward you as you move your torso closer to them at the same time. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
After a second pause, go back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Lie on an exercise mat with your legs extended and your hands either palms facing down next to you or under your glutes.  This will be your starting position.

Bend your knees and pull your upper thighs into your midsection as you breathe out. Continue the motion until your knees are around chest level. Contract your abs as you execute this movement and hold for a second at the top. Tip: As you perform the motion, the lower legs (calves) should always remain parallel to the floor.
Return to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both hold a high-cable rope near the shoulders and curl the ribcage toward the pelvis while keeping the hips steady. One sits on a bench facing away and the base kneels facing the station.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seated/kneeling accessibility and cable direction; preserve only as an explicit position option if approved.
candidates.name: Cable Seated Crunch
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with your back facing a high pulley.

Grasp the cable rope attachment with both hands (with the palms of the hands facing each other) and place your hands securely over both shoulders. Keep the trunk upright without allowing the cable to pull the back into an exaggerated arch. This will be your starting position.
With the hips stationary, flex the waist so the elbows travel toward the hips. Breathe out as you perform this step.
As you inhale, go back to the initial position slowly.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Kneel facing a high cable and hold the rope near the shoulders.
Curl the ribcage toward the pelvis without pulling with the arms, then return slowly.

candidates.rationale: Both use the same rotating dumbbell Arnold press sequence. The candidate adds a supported seat, while the base stands with a steady trunk.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seated support versus standing trunk demand was previously requested as useful variety; keep unless seating becomes an exercise modifier.
candidates.name: Seated Arnold Dumbbell Press
instructions: Sit on an exercise bench with back support and hold two dumbbells in front of you at about upper chest level with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent. Tip: Your arms should be next to your torso. The starting position should look like the contracted portion of a dumbbell curl.
Now to perform the movement, raise the dumbbells as you rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
Continue lifting the dumbbells until your arms are extended above you in straight arm position. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement.

After a second pause at the top, begin to lower the dumbbells to the original position by rotating the palms of your hands towards you. Tip: The left arm will be rotated in a counter clockwise manner while the right one will be rotated clockwise. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand with a steady trunk and dumbbells in front of the shoulders, palms facing you.
Rotate the palms forward as you press up, then reverse slowly through a comfortable shoulder range.

candidates.rationale: Both strictly press a barbell from the front shoulders overhead. The candidate sits on a supported bench; the base stands.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Supported seating and trunk demands are meaningful; previous requests explicitly valued seated variations.
candidates.name: Seated Barbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a supported bench inside a rack with the bar set where you can unrack it under control. Grasp it with a comfortable overhand grip and bring it just in front of the shoulders.
Keep the torso steady and press the bar overhead without leaning back.
Lower to the starting position under control and finish by returning the bar to the rack.
baseInstructions: Set a barbell in a rack near shoulder height. Take a grip just outside shoulder width, brace the trunk, and step back with the bar at the front of the shoulders.
Press overhead while keeping the ribs down and moving the head just enough to let the bar pass.
Lower to the front of the shoulders without leaning back, then return the bar to the rack after the set.

candidates.rationale: Both press two dumbbells from the shoulders overhead. The candidate uses a supported seat while the base stands.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain seated availability unless the product can represent seated versus standing within one exercise.
candidates.name: Seated Dumbbell Press
instructions: Grab a couple of dumbbells and sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs.
Clean the dumbbells up one at a time by using your thighs to bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height at each side.
Rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, push the dumbbells up until they touch at the top.
After a second pause, slowly come down back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold the dumbbells beside the shoulders, with wrists stacked over elbows.
Press both dumbbells overhead without arching the back, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both raise dumbbells out to shoulder height with a soft elbow bend. The candidate sits upright; the base stands.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seated setup may matter to users and was previously requested as useful variation.
candidates.name: Seated Side Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit tall on a stable bench with a dumbbell beside each thigh and a soft bend in the elbows.
Raise both arms out to about shoulder height while keeping the wrists comfortable and avoiding a shrug or swing.
Lower slowly and repeat.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with softly bent elbows and dumbbells by the sides.
Lift the arms out to about shoulder height, then lower without shrugging or swinging.

candidates.rationale: Both hold one dumbbell with two hands overhead and bend/extend the elbows behind the head. Only supported seating versus standing changes.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Keep a seated choice if posture variants remain independently selectable.
candidates.name: Seated Triceps Press
instructions: Sit down on a bench with back support and grasp a dumbbell with both hands and hold it overhead at arm's length. Tip: a better way is to have somebody hand it to you especially if it is very heavy. The resistance should be resting in the palms of your hands with your thumbs around it. The palm of the hand should be facing inward. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms close to your head (elbows in) and perpendicular to the floor, lower the resistance in a semi-circular motion behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: The upper arms should remain stationary and only the forearms should move. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Go back to the starting position by using the triceps to raise the dumbbell. Breathe out as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Stand with feet about hip width apart and hold one dumbbell securely overhead with both hands.
Bend the elbows to lower it behind the head through a comfortable range, then extend without arching the back.

candidates.rationale: Both keep the upper arms beside a forward-leaning torso and extend both dumbbells backward at the elbows. The candidate sits at the bench edge.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: The long name conceals a seated kickback; preserve seating if the catalog keeps posture variants.
candidates.name: Seated Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit down at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in both arms using a neutral grip (palms of the hand facing you).
Bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up.

The upper arms with the dumbbells should be close to the torso and aligned with it (lifted up until they are parallel to the floor while the forearms are pointing towards the floor as the hands hold the weights). Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearms and the upper arm. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to lift the weight as you exhale until the forearms are parallel to the floor and the whole arm is extended. Like many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
After a second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
baseInstructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Hinge forward with the back steady and upper arms beside the torso.
Straighten both elbows together to move the dumbbells behind you, then bend them slowly without swinging.

candidates.rationale: The candidate describes a kickback while seated using one arm. The base describes the same elbow motion while standing/hinged with both arms.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Both seating and unilateral count would change; merge only if both can be explicit options.
candidates.name: Seated Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: Sit down at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in one arm using a neutral grip (palms of the hand facing you).
Bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up.

The upper arm with the dumbbell should be close to the torso and aligned with it (lifted up until it is parallel to the floor while the forearms are pointing towards the floor as the hands hold the weights). Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearms and the upper arm. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arm stationary, use the triceps to lift the weight as you exhale until the forearm is parallel to the floor and the whole arm is extended. Like many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
After a second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Hinge forward with the back steady and upper arms beside the torso.
Straighten both elbows together to move the dumbbells behind you, then bend them slowly without swinging.

candidates.rationale: Both start with two low-cable handles at shoulder height and press them overhead. The seated version adds a stable bench and back support.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Seated support and standing balance were previously requested as distinct coverage; keep unless user chooses one exercise with position options.
candidates.name: Seated Cable Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a stable bench between low cable pulleys and position one handle near each shoulder.
Keep the back supported and trunk braced as you press both handles overhead.
Lower both handles under control to shoulder height and repeat without lifting away from the support.
baseInstructions: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight.
Stand directly in between the uprights. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press the handles directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat.

candidates.rationale: Both stand at a high cable and extend the elbow with the upper arm beside the torso. The variant uses one underhand handle instead of a bilateral rope.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Single-arm work and per-side counting; grip is an option but unilateral tracking is a separate product decision.
candidates.name: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension
instructions: With your right hand, grasp a single handle attached to the high-cable pulley using a supinated (underhand; palms facing up) grip. You should be standing directly in front of the weight stack.

Now pull the handle down so that your upper arm and elbow are locked in to the side of your body. Your upper arm and forearm should form an acute angle (less than 90-degrees). You can keep the other arm by the waist and you can have one leg in front of you and the other one back for better balance. This will be your starting position.

As you contract the triceps, move the single handle attachment down to your side until your arm is straight. Breathe out as you perform this movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Your upper arms should remain stationary at all times.
Squeeze the triceps and hold for a second in this contracted position.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform the same movement with the other arm.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand facing a high cable with a rope attachment and elbows beside the ribs.
Straighten the elbows to press the rope down, then return without moving the upper arms.

candidates.rationale: Both stand facing away from a low pulley and extend the elbows with the upper arms near the head. The variant uses one handle and free-hand elbow support instead of a two-handed rope.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Single-arm selection, support cue and per-side repetition convention.
candidates.name: Standing Low-Pulley One-Arm Triceps Extension
instructions: Grab a single handle with your left arm next to the low pulley machine. Turn away from the machine keeping the handle to the side of your body with your arm fully extended. Now use both hands to elevate the single handle directly above the head with the palm facing forward. Keep your upper arm completely vertical (perpendicular to the floor) and put your right hand on your left elbow to help keep it steady. This is the starting position.

Keeping your upper arms close to your head (elbows in) and perpendicular to the floor, lower the resistance in a semicircular motion behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: The upper arms should remain stationary and only the forearms should move. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Go back to the starting position by using the triceps to raise the single handle. Breathe out as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Attach a rope to the bottom pulley of the pulley machine.

Grasping the rope with both hands, extend your arms with your hands directly above your head using a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Your elbows should be in close to your head and the arms should be perpendicular to the floor with the knuckles aimed at the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower the rope behind your head as you hold the upper arms stationary. Inhale as you perform this movement and pause when your triceps are fully stretched.
Return to the starting position by flexing your triceps as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

candidates.rationale: Both raise a dumbbell out to shoulder height. The candidate performs one side at a time and steadies the other hand on a bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Unilateral choice and per-side counting; support itself is only a setup option.
candidates.name: One-Arm Side Laterals
instructions: Stand beside a bench and use the free hand for support while holding a dumbbell by the other side.
Keep a soft elbow bend and comfortable wrist position as you raise the arm out to about shoulder height without swinging.
Lower slowly and complete the selected repetitions on each side.
baseInstructions: Stand tall with softly bent elbows and dumbbells by the sides.
Lift the arms out to about shoulder height, then lower without shrugging or swinging.

candidates.rationale: Both use a fixed soft elbow bend to open and close a dumbbell fly on a flat bench. The candidate works one arm while the other helps balance.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Asymmetric load and per-side counting; retain unless unilateral execution becomes a modifier.
candidates.name: One-Arm Flat Bench Dumbbell Flye
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell held above the chest and the other hand resting for balance.
Maintain a soft fixed elbow bend while opening the working arm to the side through a comfortable shoulder range.
Bring the dumbbell back above the chest using the same arc. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells above the chest and elbows slightly bent.
Open the arms to a comfortable depth, then bring the weights together without changing the elbow bend.

candidates.rationale: Both use the same dumbbell flat-bench pressing path. The candidate uses one dumbbell and requires the trunk to resist asymmetric loading.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Meaningful unilateral trunk demand and per-side prescription; do not merge automatically.
candidates.name: One Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell positioned beside the chest, using the free hand to help set it in place.
Keep the feet grounded and trunk steady as you press the dumbbell above the chest, then lower under control.
Use the free hand to help recover the weight after the set. Complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other.
Then, using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. The dumbbells should be just to the sides of your chest, with your upper arm and forearm creating a 90 degree angle. Be sure to maintain full control of the dumbbells at all times. This will be your starting position.

Then, as you breathe out, use your chest to push the dumbbells up. Lock your arms at the top of the lift and squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then begin coming down slowly. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

candidates.rationale: Both raise a Smith bar by lifting the elbow outward to shoulder level and lower under control. The variant removes the other hand and uses one arm.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: One-sided machine handling and per-side counts are material; keep unless unilateral modes replace separate records.
candidates.name: Smith Machine One-Arm Upright Row
instructions: With the bar at thigh level, load an appropriate weight.

Take a wide grip on the bar and unhook the weight, removing your off hand from the bar. Your arm should be extended as you stand up straight with your head and chest up. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by flexing the elbow, raising the upper arm with the elbow pointed out. Continue until your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
After a brief pause, return the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before engaging the hooks to rack the weight.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Stand holding the Smith bar in an overhand grip with arms extended and knees soft.
Raise the elbows to guide the bar upward through a comfortable range, keeping the upper arms no higher than shoulder level.
Lower under control and rerack after the selected repetitions without forcing the bar to the chin.

candidates.rationale: Both stand at a low pulley and curl with the upper arm beside the torso and palms forward. The variant uses one handle and completes each arm separately.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain per-arm counting and loads if a shared exercise supports unilateral mode.
candidates.name: Standing One-Arm Cable Curl
instructions: Start out by grabbing single handle next to the low pulley machine. Make sure you are far enough from the machine so that your arm is supporting the weight.

Make sure that your upper arm is stationary, perpendicular to the floor with elbows in and palms facing forward. Your non lifting arm should be grabbing your waist. This will allow you to keep your balance.
Slowly begin to curl the single handle upwards while keeping the upper arm stationary until your forearm touches your bicep while exhaling. Tip: Only the forearm should move.
Hold the contraction position as you squeeze the bicep and then lower the single handle back down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms while performing this exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Face a low cable with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle while keeping the elbows near the sides, then lower under control.

candidates.rationale: Both use a standing hip hinge and extend the elbow with the upper arm beside the torso. The candidate uses one dumbbell and repeats each side; the base moves both together.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Retain per-side prescription and optional single-arm balance demand.
candidates.name: Standing Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
instructions: With a dumbbell in one hand and the palm facing your torso, bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up.

The upper arm should be close to the torso and parallel to the floor while the forearm is pointing towards the floor as the hand holds the weight. Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearm and the upper arm. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to lift the weights as you exhale until the forearms are parallel to the floor and the whole arm is extended. Like many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
After a second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Hinge forward with the back steady and upper arms beside the torso.
Straighten both elbows together to move the dumbbells behind you, then bend them slowly without swinging.

candidates.rationale: Both use a seated pulldown machine with the thigh pad secured and pull an overhead attachment toward the torso. The variant works one handle and one side at a time.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Preserve side-specific counting and the free-moving single handle if consolidation is selected.
candidates.name: One Arm Lat Pulldown
instructions: Select an appropriate weight and adjust the knee pad to help keep you down. Grasp the handle with a pronated grip. This will be your starting position.
Pull the handle down, squeezing your elbow to your side as you flex the elbow.
Pause at the bottom of the motion, and then slowly return the handle to the starting position.
For multiple repetitions, avoid completely returning the weight to keep tension on the muscles being worked.
Complete the selected repetitions on each side; when alternating, count each side toward its own target.
baseInstructions: Secure the thigh pad and grip the overhead bar.
Pull the bar toward the upper chest while keeping the torso mostly still, then let the arms extend under control.

candidates.rationale: Both sit at a low row cable with feet braced and pull toward the torso without moving the trunk. The variant rows one handle and rotates toward a neutral grip.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Single-arm mode, per-side target and handle rotation; this is conditional rather than a simple naming duplicate.
candidates.name: Seated One-arm Cable Pulley Rows
instructions: Sit at a low cable row with feet braced and one handle in the working hand. Begin with a pronated grip and the trunk steady.
Pull the handle toward the side of the torso while turning to a neutral grip, keeping the shoulders level.
Reach forward under control and complete the selected repetitions on each arm.
baseInstructions: Sit tall with feet braced and knees softly bent.
Pull the handle toward the lower ribs, then reach forward under control without rounding or rocking the torso.

candidates.variation: Single-arm wrist curl with thigh support
candidates.rationale: Both perform supported palms-up dumbbell wrist flexion. The candidate uses one arm on a thigh; the base uses both arms on a bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support is minor, but retain per-hand counting and unilateral choice.
candidates.name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with one forearm resting along the thigh, palm up and wrist free just beyond the knee, holding a dumbbell.
Curl the hand upward through a comfortable wrist range without moving the forearm.
Lower under control and complete the selected repetitions on each hand.
baseInstructions: Kneel facing a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Rest the forearms on the bench with palms upward and wrists just beyond the edge.
Curl both wrists through a small controlled range, then lower the dumbbells slowly.

candidates.variation: Single-arm wrist extension with thigh support
candidates.rationale: Both perform supported palms-down dumbbell wrist extension. The candidate uses one arm on a thigh; the base uses both arms on a bench.
candidates.distinctionToPreserve: Support is minor, but retain per-hand counting and unilateral choice.
candidates.name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with one forearm resting along the thigh, palm down and wrist free just beyond the knee, holding a dumbbell.
